rows.name: Comp2Comp spine module (Blankemeier 2023, StanfordMIMI/Comp2Comp)
rows.reason: paper: "freely available under the AGPL-3.0 License", table T12 4.93 (1.82); code: spherical = False, task_ids=[292], TS_SPINE {L5: 27 ... T12: 32}; readthedocs badge "License: GPL v3". https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2302.06568 https://raw.githubusercontent.com/StanfordMIMI/Comp2Comp/master/comp2comp/spine/spine.py https://raw.githubusercontent.com/StanfordMIMI/Comp2Comp/master/comp2comp/models/models.py https://comp2comp.readthedocs.io/en/latest/
rows.row_markdown: | Comp2Comp spine module, Blankemeier et al. 2023, arXiv 2302.06568 (github StanfordMIMI/Comp2Comp) [code: README, LICENSE, comp2comp/spine/spine.py, spine_utils.py and models/models.py read raw; paper full on ar5iv]: the paper names TotalSegmentator's spine-only nnU-Net (1,082 training CTs, C1 to L5) and keeps T12 to L5; the code's ts_spine path now calls TotalSegmentator v2's total task (task id 292) and reads six fixed keys T12, L1 to L5 from Comp2Comp's own category table (models.py TS_SPINE, label indices 27 to 32); per level a right-left centre of mass, the sagittal slice's two largest components with the posterior one (the spinous process) dropped, a 2D body centre, a 1 cm diameter sphere (optionally cubic) in the paper (an oval per-slice ROI eroded away from the cortex in the code, the spherical branch switched off by spherical = False) and its median HU in the paper (np.mean in mean_img_mask in the code) as a BMD surrogate; no height, width, depth, area or volume of any vertebra is computed; the only areas are muscle, SAT, VAT and IMAT on axial slices | Spine centres validated on 40 Stanford tertiary-centre emergency-department intravenous-contrast CTs against the authors' own body-only labels, not public; the paper does not say how the labels were made | Public; the LICENSE file is Apache 2.0 and the README badge says Apache 2.0, while the paper's text says AGPL-3.0 and the readthedocs page's badge says GPL v3 | Vertical centre absolute error, mean (median) mm: T12 4.93 (1.82), L1 5.35 (2.39), L2 4.78 (2.24), L3 3.38 (2.00), L4 2.68 (0.82), L5 4.30 (2.95); no dimension validated | T12 to L5 only; a missing label only logs a warning (compute_centroids), no relabelling for a missing or extra vertebra; a post-hoc block (process_post_hoc) that reverts the Stanford model's six labels when fewer than six bodies are found or the largest component is 1.5 times the second lies inside a commented-out string (spine_utils.py lines 655 to 885) and is never called; computes nothing of this family, so Palm 2025's heights come from Palm's own polygon code over Comp2Comp's centroid and slice |

the mm errors, the cohort details and the training recipe only from the repolab.lib.niigata-u.ac.jp AI-generated summary (page), since the repository record niigata-u.repo.nii.ac.jp/records/2001625 answers 503 under a maintenance notice dated 28 Oct 2026]: U-Net segmentation of the thoracic bodies (MATLAB; Dice 0.94 +/- 0.01 on 10 postmortem scans by leave-one-out, then retrained on their 2,116 axial images) then an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet18 regressing 36 values (depth, width, height times T1 to T12) from 8 volume-rendered views at 45 degree steps, for personal identification in mass disasters | Niigata City General Hospital, 42 patients, 84 non-contrast CTs (antemortem and postmortem pairs; the abstract itself says 84 scans), 2 mm slices; not public; truth: manual shortest depth, width and height in mm of each body T1 to T12 in Aquarius NET; 6-fold cross-validation by scan, the 8 views' predictions averaged | Not stated | Abstract: Spearman rho above 0.900 for depth and width with over 80 percent of scans within +/-10 percent, rho 0.777 for height with 70.4 percent within +/-10 percent; summary only: MAE / RMSE depth 1.45 / 1.95 mm, width 1.70 / 2.25 mm, height 1.54 / 2.32 mm, rho 0.928 and 0.902, within 10 percent 84.6 and 82.6, Bland-Altman proportional bias rho 0.277, 0.291, 0.354; no ICC | T1 to T12 only, a fixed 36-output regressor that assumes twelve thoracic bodies; forensic, half post-mortem, 42 people, a departmental bulletin; levels from the manual protocol; the one automated CT body width and depth in mm found, and its mm figures are read from a generated summary, not the paper |

rows.row_markdown: | Wilson, Whitehouse, Allen, Saunders, Wilson, Abel 2025, medRxiv 10.1101/2025.10.31.25339216 (Europe PMC PPR1112609; Imperial, Oxford, Manchester, Aberdeen) [full, the JATS source XML on medrxiv.org]: IoMSpine (Optasia Medical, Manchester) AI-assisted six-point morphometry on UK Biobank DXA spine images, measuring body heights and wedge, biconcave and crush ratios, each case reviewed by a radiographer and verified by an MSK radiologist; fracture at 20 percent or more height loss (mild 20 to 25, moderate 25 to 40, severe over 40) | UK Biobank application 17295, data to bona fide researchers through UK Biobank only: 2,446 participants aged 40 to 79 (2,466 less 20 with prior spine injury), GE iDXA software v16.00.158, scanned 2014 to 2016 at Stockport; T4 to L4; 32,058 vertebrae, 220 (0.69 percent) excluded for poor image quality, 31,798 assessed (the two counts are 2,466 and 2,446 times 13 levels, so the 220 are not subtracted from the assessed count); interobserver study 100 cases (1,287 vertebrae), the contributors statement naming RW and GA as the independent reviewers beside the primary reader, Cohen's and Fleiss' weighted kappa | Commercial (Optasia IoMSpine, version not printed); no code | No landmark or height accuracy; weighted Fleiss kappa 0.74, maximum observer discrepancy 2.6 percent at T11; the tool first flagged 4,590 vertebrae (14.4 percent), 606 reclassified as benign findings on review and 3,984 (12.5 percent of all) false positives with no alternative diagnosis; prevalence 763 of 2,446 (31.1 percent) | No per-level height table (the text gives only mid-height rising 0.70 to 0.89 mm a level from T4 to L3 and falling 0.80 mm at L4); heights and landmarks not released; DXA, T4 to L4; nothing printed on level-naming errors (the under-2-percent annotator misclassification, mostly lumbar, is of fracture against benign findings, not of level); CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 |

facts.row: Hipp, Grieco, Newman, Reitman 2022, JBMR Plus 6(10):e10677 (PMC9549721) [full on PMC]
facts.reason: Appendix 1 (s002.docx) Table 1 "35,275 lumbar vertebrae", L1 0.944[0.043], S1 1.296[0.071], EPWR S1 1.611[0.154]; Table 9 L4 to L5 VBHR 0.124[0.059]; Table 7 EPA-VBHR 0.9904; Table 5 R2 0.75 to 0.93. https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC9549721/supplementaryFiles
facts.fact: Appendix S1 (file s002.docx) tabulates per level, after trimming vertebrae with any metric beyond 2 SD, the six metrics' means and SD for 35,275 lumbar vertebrae (L1 5,870, L2 5,987, L3 5,946, L4 5,953, L5 5,886, S1 5,638) and 44,938 cervical (C2 7,705, C3 8,180, C4 8,017, C5 8,127, C6 7,695, C7 5,214), e.g. VBHR L1 0.944 [0.043] to L5 1.154 [0.066] and S1 1.296 [0.071], EPWR S1 1.611 [0.154], EPA L5 6.517 [2.655] and S1 11.937 [3.456] deg; adjacent-level absolute differences (L4 to L5 VBHR 0.124 [0.059], L5 to S1 EPWR 0.589 [0.134], C2 to C3 HWR 0.426 [0.070]); Pearson correlations between the metrics (lumbar VBHR with EPA 0.9904); and MANOVA where vertebra explains most (R2 0.75 to 0.93 lumbar). These are the ratio tables a level-naming rule could be scored against; the landmarks themselves are still not released.

facts.row: Pedicle screw planning DL, J Bone Oncol 2024 (PMC11345936) [abstract from search]
facts.reason: Table 5: axial angle ICC 0.92 and 0.93, MAE 1.614 and 1.592; path length 0.82 and 0.87, 2.242 and 1.774; width 0.97 and 0.98, 0.368 and 0.332; interpedicular 0.91, 1.254; path between "the anterior and posterior vertebral cortices passing through G". https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11345936/
facts.fact: Read in full (Zhang et al., J Bone Oncol 47:100627, already [full] in pedicles.md): its Table 5 holds seven parameters, all pedicle, screw path or interpedicular, none a body dimension: left and right pedicle axial angle ICC 0.92 and 0.93 (MAE 1.614 and 1.592 deg), left and right screw path length ICC 0.82 and 0.87 (MAE 2.242 and 1.774 mm), left and right pedicle width ICC 0.97 and 0.98 (MAE 0.368 and 0.332 mm), interpedicular distance ICC 0.91 (MAE 1.254 mm); the screw path runs between the anterior and posterior cortices along a line parallel to the pedicle but is not reported as a body depth. The row's tag can become [full] and its Lacks cell stand as written.

facts.row: Palm et al. 2025, Sci Rep 15 (PMC12218285) [full on PMC]
facts.reason: spine_utils.py: compute_centroids, roi_from_mask ("Create an oval ROI"), mean_img_mask (np.mean), process_post_hoc inside the string literal of lines 655 to 885 and never called; models.py TS_SPINE {"L5": 27, ... "T12": 32}. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/StanfordMIMI/Comp2Comp/master/comp2comp/spine/spine_utils.py https://raw.githubusercontent.com/StanfordMIMI/Comp2Comp/master/comp2comp/models/models.py
facts.fact: Comp2Comp's spine code computes per level only a centroid, a ROI and its HU (spine_utils.py: compute_centroids, compute_rois, roi_from_mask, mean_img_mask), with no height, width, depth or area; its only relabelling heuristic, process_post_hoc, which reverts the Stanford spine model's six labels when fewer than six bodies or a fused component is found, sits inside a commented-out string (lines 655 to 885) and is never called, so a missing level only logs a warning; the level names are Comp2Comp's own six keys T12, L1 to L5 (models.py TS_SPINE) mapped to TotalSegmentator's label indices 27 to 32 and passed through unchanged, so the Ha, Hc and Hp of this row are Palm's own OpenCV polygon code over Comp2Comp's centroid slice.

gaps.reader_notes: Settled, changed: the family now has one automated width and depth on CT in mm, Ichikawa 2025 (MAE 1.45 mm depth, 1.70 mm width, 1.54 mm height, T1 to T12, 42 forensic patients, read from a generated summary), so the sentence that the only such validation is Siemionow's percent figure should say that, and the automated-area gap is now a searched negative (Europe PMC, OpenAlex, WebSearch) rather than an unrun query; Comp2Comp is settled as computing centres and HU only, with TotalSegmentator's names passed through and no relabelling, so Palm's heights are Palm's own code; Alukaev 2022 adds a CT body-height MAE of 1.17 mm (which height and which levels unstated, counts matching VerSe 2019) to the bullet that CT work gives only ICC or r; Hipp 2022's appendices give no landmark accuracy in mm either, only projection sensitivity in SD units (up to 1.65 SD between flexion and extension films, 2 SD or more across DRR views for FBDR and PSA) and the per-level ratio tables with counts, which is what a film-ratio level rule would be scored against and also what limits it. Not settled, changed: the UK Biobank preprint (2,446 people, 31,798 vertebrae T4 to L4, IoMSpine, kappa 0.74) releases no heights, so public reader-measured heights by level still do not exist, and Zenodo, Hugging Face and the reachable part of Grand Challenge add none; the only reader-reader agreement for body length and width on CT is Abel 2024's manual ICC of 0.60 to 0.95 on 16 patients, which bounds any future automatic width or depth validation; Ma 2024 and Engelke 2019 stay at abstract level with no open copy, and the Ichikawa numbers need the paper itself once the Niigata repository answers.
gaps.verifier_notes: Every source was read at the URL given or at the records it points to; nothing under /home/user/bordercall was changed and nothing was fetched into git. Fetched copies are under <session scratchpad>/verify-vertebral-body/ (PubMed efetch texts, Europe PMC, OpenAlex, biorxiv and CiNii JSON, the Comp2Comp README, LICENSE, spine.py, spine_utils.py and models.py, the readthedocs page, the medRxiv JATS XML, the Niigata repolab HTML and the Hipp supplementary zip unpacked under hipp_supp/ with the three docx texts). Budget used: 5 WebFetch calls (ar5iv paper, PMC11345936 twice, the Niigata repolab page, one 429 on the medRxiv XML), 0 WebSearch; the rest by curl, which read eutils, Europe PMC, api.biorxiv.org, raw.githubusercontent.com, medrxiv.org's source XML, cir.nii.ac.jp and comp2comp.readthedocs.io; api.github.com answered 403 through the proxy and gh is not attached to that repository, so stars and pushed_at were not read (not in the row). Findings beyond the rows: (1) the Niigata University repository (niigata-u.repo.nii.ac.jp, the handle's target) answers 503 with a maintenance notice dated 28 Oct 2026, which is why the reader and I saw 503; the paper's own abstract is on CiNii (crid 1050303940570670336) and confirms 84 scans, DSC 0.94, rho above 0.900 for depth and width, rho 0.777 and 70.4 percent for height, but every mm figure, the 42 patients, the 2,116 images and the training recipe exist only in the AI-generated summary; the journal's English name on CiNii is Journal of Health Sciences of Niigata University (a second CiNii record spells it Journal of Health of NiigataUniversity), ISSN 2188-4617, a departmental bulletin paper, so the reader's Niigata Journal of Health Sciences is not at any source. (2) Wilson's vertebra counts are exactly 13 levels times the participant counts (2,466 x 13 = 32,058; 2,446 x 13 = 31,798), so the 220 poor-quality exclusions are not subtracted from the assessed count; and the contributors statement names RW and GA as the independent reviewers of the 100 cases beside the primary reader DW, with Cohen's and Fleiss' kappa, so two readers is not what the source says. (3) Comp2Comp's licence reads three ways at four sources: Apache 2.0 (LICENSE file and README badge), AGPL-3.0 (paper text), GPL v3 (readthedocs badge); and the current ts_spine path calls TotalSegmentator v2's total task 292 rather than the 2023 spine-only model the paper describes (the Stanford branch still references TotalSegmentator v1 task 252). (4) Alukaev 2022 is already tabled in end-plates.md (abstract) but not in vertebral-body.md, so the row is no duplicate of this note; the arXiv API answered 429 to me as to the reader, and OpenAlex lists only closed locations. (5) Abel's 0.60 to 0.95 ICC is pooled over VL, VW, PH and PW in the abstract, so no body-only ICC exists at the abstract level. Alukaev's claim that 160 CTs and 1,725 vertebrae equal VerSe 2019's counts matches the note's own VerSe row but the abstract names no dataset, as the row says.

reader_rows.name: Comp2Comp spine module (Blankemeier 2023, StanfordMIMI/Comp2Comp)
reader_rows.row_markdown: | Comp2Comp spine module, Blankemeier et al. 2023, arXiv 2302.06568 (github StanfordMIMI/Comp2Comp) [code: README, LICENSE and comp2comp/spine/spine_utils.py read raw; paper full on ar5iv]: TotalSegmentator's spine-only nnU-Net (1,082 training CTs, C1 to L5) gives the labels and the pipeline keeps T12 to L5; per level a right-left centre of mass, the sagittal slice's two largest components with the posterior one (the spinous process) dropped, a 2D body centre, a 1 cm sphere in the paper (an elliptical ROI in the code, the spherical branch switched off) and its median HU in the paper (mean in the code) as a BMD surrogate; no height, width, depth, area or volume of any vertebra is computed; the only area is muscle and fat on axial slices | Spine centres validated on 40 Stanford emergency-department contrast CTs against body-only labels, not public; the paper does not call the reference manual | Public; the LICENSE file is Apache 2.0 (the paper's text says AGPL-3.0, the readthedocs badge GPL v3) | Vertical centre error, mean (median) mm: T12 4.93 (1.82), L1 5.35 (2.39), L2 4.78 (2.24), L3 3.38 (2.00), L4 2.68 (0.82), L5 4.30 (2.95); no dimension validated | T12 to L5 only; level names are the segmenter's category keys, a missing label only logs a warning, no relabelling for a missing or extra vertebra (an inactive post-hoc block reverts to the original labels when fewer than 6 bodies are predicted); computes nothing of this family, so Palm 2025's heights come from Palm's own polygon code over Comp2Comp's centroid and slice |
reader_rows.where_in_note: Table, after the Palm et al. 2025 row (Palm builds on it)
reader_rows.why_it_matters: Settles the open Gaps question: Comp2Comp finds levels from TotalSegmentator and computes centres and HU only, never a height, width or depth, so no public pipeline on CT gives this family's measures out of the box.

reader_rows.row_markdown: | Ichikawa, Kondo, Okamoto, Kondo, Takahashi 2025, Niigata Journal of Health Sciences 21(1):10-20 (repolab.lib.niigata-u.ac.jp record 2001625; hdl 10191/0002001625) [page: the repository's generated summary, since the paper's own record and PDF answered 503 three times]: U-Net segmentation of the thoracic bodies (MATLAB, Dice 0.94 on 10 scans, retrained on 2,116 axial images) then a ResNet18 regressing 36 values (depth, width, height times T1 to T12) from 8 volume-rendered views at 45 degree steps, for personal identification in mass disasters | Niigata City General Hospital, 42 patients, 84 non-contrast CTs (antemortem and postmortem pairs), 2 mm slices; not public; truth: manual shortest depth, width and height of each body T1 to T12 in Aquarius NET; 6-fold cross-validation by scan | Not stated | MAE / RMSE depth 1.45 / 1.95 mm, width 1.70 / 2.25 mm, height 1.54 / 2.32 mm; Spearman 0.928, 0.902, 0.777; within 10 percent of manual 84.6, 82.6, 70.4 percent; weak proportional bias (rho 0.277 to 0.354); no ICC | T1 to T12 only, a fixed 36-output regressor that assumes twelve thoracic bodies; pilot, forensic, half post-mortem; levels from the manual protocol; the one automated CT body width and depth in mm found, and its numbers are read from a generated summary, not the paper |

reader_facts.row: Engelke, Stampa, Steiger, Fuerst, Genant 2019, Arch Osteoporos 14:18 [abstract]

reader_facts.fact: Appendix S3 (file s001.docx) is projection error with exact landmarks: 26 lumbar CTs (1 mm or thinner, resampled to 0.2 mm), the four landmarks digitised in 3D in Slicer for L1 to S1, 41 DRRs a CT through Plastimatch (40 inch source-to-image, isocentre at L3, tilts +/-10 deg sagittal and axial, shifts +/-2 end-plate widths AP and LR and +/-3 cranio-caudal, rotations +/-24 deg); median (95th percentile) range of each standardised metric over the 41 views: EPA 0.3658 (1.0796), EPWR 0.6643 (2.2362), FBDR 2.4421 (4.1485), HWR 0.6378 (1.1342), PSA 2.1198 (3.7636), VBHR 0.3628 (1.2465) SD; the DRRs were judged below clinical quality and not used to validate the networks.

reader_facts.row: Hipp, Grieco, Newman, Reitman 2022, JBMR Plus 6(10):e10677 (PMC9549721) [full on PMC]
reader_facts.fact: Appendix S1 (file s002.docx) tabulates per level, after trimming vertebrae with any metric beyond 2 SD, the six metrics' means and SD for 35,275 lumbar vertebrae (L1 5,870, L2 5,987, L3 5,946, L4 5,953, L5 5,886, S1 5,638) and 44,938 cervical (C2 7,705, C3 8,180, C4 8,017, C5 8,127, C6 7,695, C7 5,214), e.g. VBHR L1 0.944 [0.043] to L5 1.154 [0.066] and S1 1.296 [0.071], EPWR S1 1.611 [0.154], EPA L5 6.517 [2.655] and S1 11.937 [3.456] deg; adjacent-level absolute differences (L4 to L5 VBHR 0.124 [0.059], L5 to S1 EPWR 0.589 [0.134], C2 to C3 HWR 0.426 [0.070]); Pearson correlations between the metrics (lumbar VBHR with EPA 0.9904); and MANOVA where vertebra explains most (R2 0.75 to 0.93 lumbar). reader_facts.row: Pedicle screw planning DL, J Bone Oncol 2024 (PMC11345936) [abstract from search]

reader_facts.row: Palm et al. 2025, Sci Rep 15 (PMC12218285) [full on PMC]
reader_facts.fact: Comp2Comp's spine code computes per level only a centroid, a ROI and its HU (spine_utils.py: compute_centroids, compute_rois, roi_from_mask, mean_img_mask), with no height, width, depth or area and no relabelling heuristic, so the Ha, Hc and Hp of this row are Palm's own OpenCV polygon code over Comp2Comp's centroid slice, and the level names are TotalSegmentator's keys passed through unchanged.

gaps.reader_notes: Settled gains two things: Knez and Vrtovec 2020 is now read whole, so the family has one published per-level pedicle table from an automatic method (width, height, chord, length, both angulations and area for T1 to T12 on 540 pedicles of 26 adolescents with deformity, one non-radiologist observer, Valdoltra, CC BY-NC paper, private data), and the geometric baseline Da Mutten names is identified as Blomenkamp's EMBC 2025 skeletonization partition, public in SpineToolkit without a licence and without a pedicle class. Not settled stands: still no automatic pedicle measure in mm against a reader on a public set (Europe PMC's 235 automatic-morphometry hits add only Siemionow 2020's percent-only diameter and angulation and Vosko 2026's unreported cervical width from TotalSegmentator masks), the MRI and synthetic-CT route is entirely reader-measured (Ogihara 2026 bias 0.09 mm with limits of +/- 1.2 mm, Abel 2024, Morbee 2021, Roberts 2023 up to 34 percent axial error), the 2026 review's 14 studies hold no measurer the note lacked, and Burgin's GNN has no code. New for the public-truth column: LumbarSeg-6K (5,952 lumbar vertebrae with a pedicle class, CC BY-NC-SA), vertebra-xray-core (MIT, a 394-vertebra VerSe pedicle centroid table), Yang 2025 as the first planner trained on CTSpine1K, Massalimova 2025's 1.58 mm pedicle-centre error on public SpineDepth, and Goerres' SpineWeb sets 2 and 5 obtainable again from Zenodo 7049844 and Ljubljana, so a public pedicle-axis benchmark is now feasible.

reader_facts.row: Knez and Vrtovec 2020 Image Anal Stereol, same model as morphometry [abstract]
reader_facts.fact: Now [full] (the journal PDF extracted with pdftotext): 26 patients, 13 male and 13 female, mean age 17.1 years (12 to 34), 23 adolescent idiopathic scoliosis and 3 Scheuermann's kyphosis, scanned before screw surgery at Orthopaedic Hospital Valdoltra, Slovenia (GE LightSpeed VTC, pixel 0.25 to 0.40 mm, slice 0.6 mm, IRB approved); 270 vertebrae T1 to T12, 540 pedicles, 20 (T1) to 52 (T8, T10, T11) per level; the manual truth is one blinded observer, a medical imaging researcher, not a radiologist; the data are private and no data or code statement is made; funded by the Slovenian Research Agency P2-0232 and J2-7118.

reader_facts.row: Knez and Vrtovec 2020 Image Anal Stereol, same model as morphometry [abstract]
reader_facts.fact: Correction of the comparison numbers: manual orthogonal MPRs differ from manual oblique MPRs by 0.77 +/- 0.56 mm (ICC 0.862) for width and 1.31 +/- 1.08 mm (0.860) for height, and from the 3D computerized values by 0.74 +/- 0.57 mm (0.863) and 1.45 +/- 1.10 mm (0.840), p <= 0.0011 in each; oblique manual against computerized is 0.44 +/- 0.35 mm (ICC 0.946, p 0.37), 0.56 +/- 0.52 mm (0.970, 0.34) and chord 1.72 +/- 1.29 mm (0.962, 0.12). The note's "per-pedicle values not published" should read: per-level means and SDs are tabulated for T1 to T12 in Table 1 (manual orthogonal, manual oblique and computerized width, height and chord) and Table 2 (computerized length, sagittal angulation, transverse angulation and area), e.g. computerized width 7.9 +/- 1.4 mm at T1, 5.4 +/- 1.0 at T4, 8.8 +/- 1.7 at T12; height 9.4 +/- 2.2 at T1 to 16.9 +/- 2.4 at T12; transverse angulation 25.4 +/- 5.7 degrees at T1 to 1.1 +/- 7.3 at T12; sagittal 9.5 +/- 6.6 to 3.2 +/- 4.4; area 62.8 +/- 20.0 to 121.0 +/- 31.6 mm2; length 15.8 +/- 2.1 to 23.1 +/- 3.9 mm; ranges 2.2 to 15.1 mm width, 5.1 to 24.9 mm height, 22.6 to 69.9 mm chord. The angles and area still have no manual comparator.

reader_facts.row: Knez and Vrtovec 2020 Image Anal Stereol, same model as morphometry [abstract]
reader_facts.fact: The paper is CC BY-NC 4.0 (Crossref licence record, issued 2020-06-08); the journal is not indexed in Europe PMC, so no Europe PMC record exists; the Crossref abstract agrees with the note's figures.

reader_facts.row: Goerres 2017 Phys Med Biol, deformable atlas [full]
reader_facts.fact: Section 2.4 names the two SpineWeb sets: dataset 2 is Yao et al. 2012, MICCAI, "Detection of Vertebral Body Fractures Based on Cortical Shell Unwrapping", 10 thoracolumbar binary segmentations (used for T7, T8 and L3); dataset 5 is Ibragimov et al. 2014, IEEE Trans Med Imaging 33:861-874, 10 lumbar cases; 20 T7/T8 and 20 L3 surfaces, all from CT; no slice thickness and no code or atlas availability statement. Both are obtainable: dataset 2 within Zenodo 7049844 (Lessmann 2016, ODC-By, the 20 CSI 2014 scans "published ... on SpineWeb (datasets 2 and 15)", cite Yao 2016 CMIG 49:16-28) and dataset 5 as ten subject zips at lit.fe.uni-lj.si/en/research/resources/lumbar-CT-vertebrae/ (CC BY-NC-ND, direct download).

reader_facts.row: Burgin 2023 arXiv 2308.02509, GNN identification with the VID dataset [full, page]
reader_facts.fact: No method code exists: the MICCAI 2023 paper page's "Link to the code repository" is the dataset repository itself (github.com/ImFusionGmbH/VID-vertebra-identification-dataset) and its second dataset link, osf.io/nqjyw, is VerSe 2019's own OSF node; the arXiv HTML names only the dataset. The repository's default branch is main with Readme.md (raw README.md paths 404), folders KeypointGroundTruthNoSacrum and KeypointPredictionsNoSacrum of JSON keypoints (world_space coordinates, keypoint_type body, left, right; spine_level in the truth), mapping-export-Training.txt and -Validation.txt, LICENSE.txt; no sacral keypoints, no mention of T13, L6 or S2 on the page. The paper reports 1,949 training and 169 validation scans with no separate test set and a 47-scan hard subset: joint GNN identification 97.19 (full) and 89.88 percent (hard), VerSe 93.26 and 93.02 percent, mean keypoint error d_mean 1.68 and 1.95 (2,118 set) and 1.28 and 1.43 (VerSe) with no unit printed; the pedicle post-processing is still described only as post-processing of the VerSe segmentations.

reader_facts.row: Caprara et al. 2022, Comput Methods Biomech Biomed Engin 25(4):464-474, and Tsagkaris et al. 2023 [search only] (section 2 bullet)
reader_facts.fact: Caprara 2022 is now [abstract] (Europe PMC, PMID 34369827, Taylor and Francis, no PMC): 4 cadaveric spines (2 female, 2 male, 60 to 78 years), 20 lumbar vertebrae L1 to L5, 40 screws, genetic algorithm with finite elements, 26 percent higher simulated pull-out, no data or code statement. Tsagkaris 2023 is [full] (PMC10639121, CC BY): 5 cadavers, 25 vertebrae L1 to L5, 50 screws, the datasets "not readily available" and requested from the Spine Biomechanics Unit, Balgrist, no code; optimized median pull-out 698.7 N against 900.6 N traditional, the gain only in the subset with E-modulus times volume over 3500 MPa cm3; optimized screws 40 mm and 7 mm against 50 mm and 6 mm; no pedicle width. A web search found no repository for either; the ETH research collection record (handle 20.500.11850/500990) answered HTTP 500.

reader_facts.row: Da Mutten 2026 J Imaging Inform Med, nnU-Net subregions [abstract]
reader_facts.fact: The geometric method it compares to is Blomenkamp, Kramer, Bauer and Paulus 2025, EMBC, doi 10.1109/EMBC58623.2025.11254383, PMID 41336765, a skeletonization partition of a vertebra surface into body, laminae and processes with no pedicle class (public code in SpineToolkit's ShapeSegmentation module, no licence), which is why its Dice is reported for corpus and pedicle together.

rows.name: Fujimori 2022 cervical lordosis (Sci Rep 12:15732, PMC9492662)
rows.reason: Counts, MAEs, reader comparison, MIT LICENSE all at source. Two fixes: paper says C7 hidden means 'used the C6 vertebral endplate as a reference' (lower end-plate not stated). The 35 large errors are called 'vertebral body misidentification': hardly visible C7 12, severe deformity 8, posterior instrumented fusion 7, fused vertebrae 6, infancy 2. So level misidentification is the main failure, against the why_it_matters claim. Read via Europe PMC fullTextXML PMC9492662; raw README and LICENSE of ykszk/c2c7demo.
rows.row_markdown: | Fujimori 2022 C2-C7 angle (Osaka University) [full] | 4,546 lateral cervical films (flexion, neutral, extension) of 1,674 patients (707 men, 967 women, age 2-96), Osaka University, no patient excluded for deformity or instrumentation; truth: anterior and posterior ends of the C2 and C7 inferior end-plates by a surgeon of 18 years, checked by one of 20 years (123 corrections proposed, 5 settled with two further surgeons, all congenitally fused at C2); images from the corresponding author on request, not public [full] | Yes: github.com/ykszk/c2c7demo, LICENSE file MIT (Yuki Suzuki 2022), README names no licence; ONNX weights on Google Drive; web demo ykszk.github.io/c2c7demo [code] | DeepLabV3 + EfficientNet-B4 heat maps of four landmarks (the two ends of the C2 and C7 inferior end-plates); 5-fold CV by patient: C2-C7 MAE 3.3 (SD 4.7, median 2.2), C2 slope 1.7, C7 slope 2.7 deg; vs two surgeons on 168 patients (415 films): AI 3.1 +/- 3.4, surgeons 3.9 and 3.8 deg; no ICC [full] | Cervical only; no level label is output, the network places C2 and C7 points directly; when C7 is hidden by the shoulder the truth uses the C6 end-plate as reference; of 35 patients with errors of 20 deg or more the paper names the cause vertebral body misidentification: hardly visible C7 12, severe deformity 8, posterior instrumented fusion 7, fused vertebrae 6, infancy 2 [full] |

facts.row: AASCE 2019 challenge (Wang 2021, MedIA review), table row and the section 1 bullets 'What AASCE is'
facts.reason: Read the same Erasmus PDF (pure.eur.nl, 22 pages). All numbers held. One fix: the paper says 'five teams provided their GitHub code, as shown in Table 3'. Footnotes add ErasmusMC, PAT and, in Team UC's section, github.com/radiology-guru/cobb-angles. So eight teams carry a link, not seven. Added: 'the testing set only provides the Cobb angles as the ground truth'.
facts.fact: Read from the Erasmus repository copy (pure.eur.nl; Med Image Anal 2021;72:102115; the data section, Table 2, the Tencent section, Table 3 and its footnotes, Table 4 and the limitations) [full]. 707 AP films collected from London Health Sciences Center in Canada with the EOS system, 609 training and 98 test, IRB with Wang 2019 (Med Image Anal 58:101542) and Chen 2019 (IEEE Access 7:124596); landmarks 'provided by two professional doctors' at LHSC, four corners on 17 thoracic and lumbar vertebrae, 68 points; training angles computed from the landmarks by the organisers' Matlab code on spineweb (largest pairwise angle, then the two above and below); the test set gives only the three Cobb angles as truth; no inter-reader agreement figure for the truth in the text; JPG, Table 2 printing 72 DPI and 'Pixels dimensions (SI units, micron) 144', image length 973-3755 px (train) and 985-7316 (test), width 355-1427 and 273-2748; Cobb range 0-156.39 (train) and 0-60.93 (test); severity train 20 under 10 deg, 190 mild, 205 moderate, 194 severe, test 11, 58, 26, 3; films with steel nails 53 and 4; the authors say test and training differ in distribution and the JPG gives a somewhat lower resolution; Table 4 (SMAPE, CMAE, ED, MD, CD): Tencent 21.71, 4.85, 11.17, 14.55, 10.16; XMU 22.18, 4.91, 11.23, 14.74, 10.17; iFLYTEK 22.17, 5.48; ErasmusMC 22.96, 5.69; XDU 24.8, 6.28; PAT 25.48, 6.58; NAAMII 25.7, 6.69; UC 45.99, 17.13; Wilcoxon tests found no method significantly better than all others; the paper says five teams gave code (Table 3: XMU github.com/wangshuxinxinxin/SCG-Net, Tencent github.com/hust-linyi/Seg4Reg, iFLYTEK github.com/YJY-CV/Spine, XDU github.com/zzs95/AASCE2019_code, NAAMII github.com/Bidur-Khanal/SpineCurvEst), and footnotes in the method sections add ErasmusMC github.com/fpgdubost/aasce_emc, PAT github.com/PASpine/Xspine and, in Team UC's section, github.com/radiology-guru/cobb-angles; no data licence or download term is stated in the text.

facts.row: Seg4Reg / Seg4Reg+ (Lin), table row and the section 1 bullet
facts.reason: Raw README: 'official solution of 1st place in MICCAI 2019 AASCE Challenge', cites pp 69-74, no licence; LICENSE, LICENSE.md, LICENSE.txt all 404. OpenAlex: LNCS doi 10.1007/978-3-030-39752-4_7, pp 69-74, no abstract. Semantic Scholar batch: 41 citations, abstract elided. MedIA Tencent section matches every detail (PSPNet, ResNet-101, dilation 2, 4, 6, gradient reversal, 1024 x 512, 512 x 256, 4 P40). arXiv API 2208.12462: 'Accepted by MICCAI 2021', no number, no code link.
facts.fact: Code is public: github.com/hust-linyi/Seg4Reg, whose README calls it the official first-place solution of the MICCAI 2019 AASCE challenge and cites Lin, Zhou, Ma, Yang, Zheng, CSI 2019 pp 69-74 (LNCS, doi 10.1007/978-3-030-39752-4_7); the repository has no LICENSE file (404) and the README names no licence, weights or data. From the MedIA review [full]: Team Tencent's method modifies PSPNet (ResNet-101, dilation 2, 4, 6) to segment vertebrae and intervertebral space, then regresses the angles with ResNet, DenseNet and EfficientNet ensembles under a gradient-reversal domain adaptation, with histogram equalisation, inputs 1024 x 512 and 512 x 256, 4 P40 GPUs; SMAPE 21.71, CMAE 4.85, ED 11.17, MD 14.55, CD 10.16, first on all five metrics. The LNCS abstract itself is unreachable (Springer closed; OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar hold no abstract; Semantic Scholar counts 41 citations). Seg4Reg+ on arXiv 2208.12462 [abstract]: 'Accepted by MICCAI 2021', no number and no code link in the abstract or comments.

facts.row: Vertebra-Focused (Yi 2020), table row, and the MMA-Net bullet in section 1
facts.reason: MMA-Net HTML refs: [6] Kim KC et al., IEEE Access 8:84618-84630; [20] Guo et al. EMBC 2021; [8] Wang, Huang, Wang CSI 2019 pp 107-112. The fact calls LaNet's VfNet unresolved, but LaNet's ref [48] is Yi et al., ISBI 2020 pp 736-740. MMA-Net's authors are Qiu Z, Yang J, Wang J (arXiv HTML; OpenAlex ICRA 2024 pp 9139-9145), not 'Zhao et al.' as the note says.
facts.fact: The 'VF' of MMA-Net's Table II (MAE 3.51, SMAPE 7.84) is MMA-Net's reference 6, Kim KC, Yun HS, Kim S, Seo JK, 'Automation of spine curve assessment in frontal radiographs using deep learning of vertebral-tilt vector', IEEE Access 8:84618-84630, 2020 (Centroid-net and M-net), not Yi et al.'s network, so the row's '7.84 and MAE 3.51 deg (128 split, via MMA-Net)' belongs to Kim 2020 [full]. Yi 2020's own figure stays SMAPE 10.81 on its own 116-film split; LaNet (arXiv 2405.19645) [full] names Yi 2020 as its 'VfNet' (reference 48, ISBI 2020 pp 736-740): on the 128-film validation split SMAPE 10.48, CMAE 4.48, ED 8.92, MD 13.43, CD 7.33, and on the 98 test films, against LaNet's own landmarks, SMAPE 17.71, CMAE 5.85. MMA-Net's authors are Qiu Z, Yang J, Wang J (arXiv HTML; OpenAlex), not Zhao et al. as the note's section 1 bullet says; OpenAlex lists it as ICRA 2024 pp 9139-9145, doi 10.1109/ICRA57147.2024.10610928 [page]. Its other references: SCG-Net is Wang S, Huang S, Wang L, CSI 2019 pp 107-112; KEF is Guo Y, Li Y, He W, Song H, EMBC 2021 pp 2588-2591; MMA-Net's HTML carries no code statement or repository link.

facts.row: Doerr 2020 CT GSA, table row and the section 3 bullet
facts.reason: PMC page (2 WebFetch reads; Europe PMC XML gave 500) holds the counts and figures. Fixes: the paper says 'Seven patient CT images were used from SpineWeb Dataset 14' and never calls them public. The bounds exceed the CI at T1 and S1 for end-plate angles; for alignment measures the exceptions are PThK and ThK. The 'all GSA within the CI' clause was not confirmed in what was read. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7218103/
facts.fact: Read whole on PMC [full]. Seven patient CTs from SpineWeb Dataset 14 (the paper does not call them public), rendered to lateral and AP DRRs spanning C7 to S1; the vertebral point labels 'were defined manually by an expert radiologist' at each centroid and are inputs to both methods; five clinicians (two radiologists, three spinal neurosurgeons) annotated the end-plates; measures LL, main and proximal thoracic kyphosis, lumbar, main and proximal thoracic Cobb, PI, PI-LL, SVA, PT and ThK; mean absolute end-plate angle difference 1.9 deg (EndSeg) and 2.7 deg (SpNorm) (Table 5, at T2, T3, T4, T8, L1, L3, S1); 93.8 percent of end-plate angles inside the inter-reader 95 percent CI, which is 5.8 deg for an end-plate, 8.2 PThK, 6.0 MThK, 7.4 LL, 4.8 LC; LL, PI and PT within 3.0 deg, SVA within about 10 mm, ThK up to about 6 deg; t-test p 0.33 (EndSeg) and 0.83 (SpNorm); SpNorm takes S2 as an extra inferior control point; under label perturbation the 95 percent bounds exceed the inter-reader CI at T1 and S1 for end-plate angles, and for PThK and ThK among the alignment measures; no data or code statement (NIH R01-EB-017226 acknowledged); transitional vertebrae not mentioned, butterfly vertebra and ankylosing spondylitis named as future work. So the row's 'counts not read' becomes 7 SpineWeb CTs, level labels from one radiologist given as input, end-plates from five readers.

facts.fact: The paper is Klinwichit P, Yookwan W, Limchareon S, Chinnasarn K, Jang JS, Onuean A, 'BUU-LSPINE: A Thai Open Lumbar Spine Dataset for Spondylolisthesis Detection', Applied Sciences 2023;13(15):8646, 2023-07-27, CC BY, 36 citations on OpenAlex, 37 on Semantic Scholar; it is not indexed by Europe PMC and its only open copy is MDPI's, which refuses this container. The project page gives three releases: a 400-pair v0.1 sample (400 patients, 127 male, 273 female, ages 6 to 89, mean 50.2125; direct download), BUU-LSPINE(2000) with side-bending, rotation and flexion/extension labels (Google Drive), and BUU-LSPINE(3600) by a Google Form under an end-user licence agreement with the Faculty of Informatics, Burapha University; the annotation is the upper and lower edge lines of each lumbar vertebra as point coordinates in CSV with four listhesis diagnoses on the lower edges; JPG of various resolutions with no pixel spacing or mm statement; the GitHub README (North-Github/BUU-LSPINE) gives 3,600 patients, 7,200 images, 621 spondylolisthesis patients with 788 locations, 18.5 GB, a Google Drive folder, annotation by Burapha University Hospital physicians and radiologists, grant KSN1823130, and no licence.

gaps.reader_notes: Settled, strengthened: the AASCE truth is two doctors' corners at London Health Sciences Center on EOS films with no inter-reader figure anywhere in the official review, the test set skews mild (3 of 98 severe) and differs in distribution from training, and the 2019 leaderboard (21.71) no longer describes the state of the art (LaNet 8.99 on the same 98 films, 4.51 on the 128 split); the coronal line still names no level and still gives corner error only in px, though Table 2's 72 DPI and 144 micron entry is the first printed pixel figure, as JPG metadata rather than a calibration. Public code rises from one licensed method to two (Fujimori 2022, MIT, with weights) plus seven unlicensed AASCE team repositories, and the sagittal line gains one public external test set with reader truth, CLX-34 (1,307 cervical films, CC BY-NC-SA), on which Kang 2026 reaches ICC 0.97 for C2-C7 lordosis while the two experts agree at only 0.67 on C7 slope; the commercial EOS and Keops routes turn out to be reader-driven reconstructions (15 min a spine, levels traced by hand, Rehm excluding LSTV before the study), with inter-reader PI 3.1 and SS 2.7 deg, the same size as the deep-learning errors. Not settled stays as it was: nothing read decides a level from an angle (Kang's C7 localiser predicts C7's place from C3-C6, which is counting; Doerr takes manual centroid labels; Suri skips L6; Spinal-AI2024 and MRSpineSeg assume their counts), and the one new reproducibility figure for sagittal truth (C7 slope ICC 0.67 between experts) says the readers' own disagreement at the cervicothoracic junction exceeds the model's.
gaps.verifier_notes: Every source was read by this checker. Routes: Europe PMC fullTextXML (Fujimori PMC9492662, Kang PMC13031614, Rehm PMC5289552, Kim PMC6250964, Sadu PMC13538668); PMC pages by WebFetch for Doerr PMC7218103 (Europe PMC XML gave 500) and Suri PMC8823454; arXiv HTML (2405.19645 LaNet, 2309.13817 MMA-Net, 2411.12604 CurvNet); the arXiv API (2208.12462); the Dataverse API (CLX-34); OpenAlex work-by-DOI records (its search endpoint was out of budget); PubMed efetch (VLTENet, KEOPS); Europe PMC search (sterEOS papers, BUU); a Semantic Scholar batch; raw GitHub READMEs and LICENSE probes; the BUU project page; and the Erasmus PDF of the AASCE review through pdftotext. The GitHub API refused this session, so repository contents and licence metadata were read only through raw files. Calls used: 3 WebFetch, 0 WebSearch. The scratch folder verify-alignment already held the earlier reader's downloads; this checker's own copies are under verify-alignment/own and were the only ones used. Four things the note gets wrong beyond these rows: (1) its section 1 bullet credits MMA-Net to 'Zhao et al.', but the authors are Qiu Z, Yang J and Wang J. (2) Its table row for Vertebra-Focused (Yi 2020) carries Kim 2020's SMAPE 7.84 and MAE 3.51, while LaNet gives Yi 2020 10.48 and 4.48 on the 128 split. (3) The AASCE review calls the annotators 'two professional doctors', while the note's row says radiologists, following Chen et al. (4) LaNet's 98-film test truth is its own annotation, so no paper read scores the 98 test films against the official truth except the 2019 entrants. One finding bears on level naming: CurvNet attributes 29 of 37 large PT Cobb errors on AASCE to cervical vertebrae detected as thoracic. With Fujimori's 'vertebral body misidentification' as the main cause of large cervical errors, these are two alignment papers whose own error analyses name a wrong level as the dominant failure. MRSpineSeg is no longer downloadable from its host (Sadu 2026).

reader_rows.why_it_matters: Shows that the commercial EOS route raises reader agreement above manual (inter-rater 0.79 to 0.84 against 0.42 to 0.55) but is still reported pooled, so no PI, SS or LL error in degrees exists for it.

reader_facts.row: AASCE 2019 challenge (Wang 2021, MedIA review), table row and the section 1 bullets 'What AASCE is'
reader_facts.fact: Read from the Erasmus repository copy (repub.eur.nl/pub/136086, served from pure.eur.nl; the data section, the Tencent section, the code paragraph and table, Table 4 and the limitations). 707 AP films 'collected from London Health Sciences Center in Canada using EOS medical imaging system', 609 training and 98 test, IRB with Wang 2019 (Med Image Anal 58:101542) and Chen 2019 (IEEE Access 7:124596); landmarks 'provided by two professional doctors' at LHSC, four corners on 17 thoracic and lumbar vertebrae, 68 points; no inter-reader agreement or reliability figure for the truth anywhere in the text; the three angles come from the organisers' Matlab code on spineweb (largest pairwise angle, then the two above and below); JPG at 72 DPI with Table 2 printing 'Pixels dimensions (SI units, micron) 144', image length 973-3755 px (train) and 985-7316 (test), width 355-1427 and 273-2748; Cobb range 0-156.39 (train) and 0-60.93 (test); severity train 20 under 10 deg, 190 mild, 205 moderate, 194 severe, test 11, 58, 26, 3; films with steel nails 53 and 4; the authors say the test set differs in distribution from training and the JPG resolution is 'somewhat lower'; Table 4 leaderboard (SMAPE, CMAE, ED, MD, CD): Tencent 21.71, 4.85, 11.17, 14.55, 10.16; XMU 22.18, 4.91, 11.23, 14.74, 10.17; iFLYTEK 22.17, 5.48; ErasmusMC 22.96, 5.69; XDU 24.8, 6.28; PAT 25.48, 6.58; NAAMII 25.7, 6.69; UC 45.99, 17.13; no method was statistically better than all others by Wilcoxon; code from seven teams is linked (Table 3 and footnotes): XMU github.com/wangshuxinxinxin/SCG-Net, Tencent github.com/hust-linyi/Seg4Reg, iFLYTEK github.com/YJY-CV/Spine, XDU github.com/zzs95/AASCE2019_code, NAAMII github.com/Bidur-Khanal/SpineCurvEst, ErasmusMC github.com/fpgdubost/aasce_emc, PAT github.com/PASpine/Xspine; no data licence or download term is stated in the text.

reader_facts.row: Seg4Reg / Seg4Reg+ (Lin), table row and the section 1 bullet
reader_facts.fact: Code is public: github.com/hust-linyi/Seg4Reg, whose README calls it the official first-place solution of the MICCAI 2019 AASCE challenge and cites Lin, Zhou, Ma, Yang, Zheng, CSI 2019 pp 69-74 (LNCS, doi 10.1007/978-3-030-39752-4_7); the repository has no LICENSE file (404) and the README names no licence, weights or data. From the MedIA review [full]: Team Tencent's method modifies PSPNet (ResNet-101, dilation 2, 4, 6) to segment vertebrae and intervertebral space, then regresses the angles with ResNet, DenseNet and EfficientNet ensembles under a gradient-reversal domain adaptation, with histogram equalisation, inputs 1024 x 512 and 512 x 256, 4 P40 GPUs; SMAPE 21.71, CMAE 4.85, ED 11.17, MD 14.55, CD 10.16, first on all five metrics. The LNCS abstract itself is unreachable (Springer closed; OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar hold no abstract; Semantic Scholar counts 41 citations). Seg4Reg+ on arXiv 2208.12462 [abstract]: 'Accepted by MICCAI 2021', no number and no code link in the abstract or comments.

reader_facts.row: Vertebra-Focused (Yi 2020), table row, and the MMA-Net bullet in section 1
reader_facts.fact: The 'VF' of MMA-Net's Table II (MAE 3.51, SMAPE 7.84) is not Yi et al.'s Vertebra-Focused network: MMA-Net's reference is K. C. Kim, H. S. Yun, S. Kim, J. K. Seo, 'Automation of spine curve assessment in frontal radiographs using deep learning of vertebral-tilt vector', IEEE Access 8:84618-84630, 2020 (Centroid-net and M-net), so the row's '7.84 and MAE 3.51 deg (128 split, via MMA-Net)' belongs to Kim 2020, and Yi 2020's own figure stays SMAPE 10.81 on its own split; LaNet (arXiv 2405.19645) [full] gives a 'VfNet' SMAPE 10.48 (validation) and 17.71 (test), whose reference was not resolved. MMA-Net's other references: SCG-Net is Wang, Huang, Wang, CSI 2019 pp 107-112; KEF is Guo, Li, He, Song, EMBC 2021 pp 2588-2591; MMA-Net's HTML carries no code statement or repository link, and OpenAlex lists it as ICRA 2024 pp 9139-9145.

reader_facts.row: Doerr 2020 CT GSA, table row and the section 3 bullet
reader_facts.fact: Read whole on PMC. Seven patient CTs from the public SpineWeb Dataset 14, rendered to lateral and AP DRRs spanning C7 to S1; the vertebral point labels (centroids) 'were defined manually by an expert radiologist'; five clinicians (two radiologists, three spinal neurosurgeons) annotated the end-plates; measures PThK, MThK, LL, lumbar Cobb, main and proximal thoracic Cobb, with PI, PI-LL, SVA, PT and ThK in the results; mean absolute end-plate angle difference from manual EndSeg 1.9 deg and SpNorm 2.7 deg (Table 5, at T2, T3, T4, T8, L1, L3, S1); 93.8 percent of end-plate angles and all GSA measures inside the inter-reader 95 percent CI, which is 5.8 deg for an end-plate, 8.2 PThK, 6.0 MThK, 7.4 LL, 4.8 LC; LL, PI and PT within 3.0 deg, SVA within about 10 mm, ThK up to about 6 deg; t-test p 0.33 (EndSeg) and 0.83 (SpNorm); SpNorm takes S2 as an extra inferior control point; T1 and S1 are where the sensitivity bounds exceed the CI; no data availability or code statement on the page (NIH R01-EB-017226 acknowledged); transitional vertebrae not mentioned, butterfly vertebra and ankylosing spondylitis named as future work. So the row's 'counts not read' becomes 7 public CTs, truth from one radiologist's labels and five readers' end-plates.

reader_facts.row: Suri 2022 MR, CT, radiograph, table row and the section 3 bullet
reader_facts.fact: Read whole on PMC: no data availability or code availability statement appears in the text; lumbar lordosis is measured from the L1 bottom corners to the L5 top corners in the Methods while the Discussion says 'to the bottom of L5'; level labels come from the annotators ('six landmarks for each visible vertebral body'), with no automatic naming; C1 and C2 excluded because the middle height cannot be placed, 'L6 was not annotated when present', no cervical radiographs; CT is 60 VerSe 2019 public phase 1 and 2 scans plus 100 institutional; test 225 MR, 27 CT, 97 radiographs; LL MAE 2.90, 2.26 and 3.60 deg; whether the model or the institutional data are released is not said. The vertebral-body note already carries most of this [full on PMC]; the alignment row's 'availability not read' and 'level method not read' are now 'not stated' and 'from the annotation'.

reader_facts.row: Section 2, 'Public truth for the sagittal family', the bullet 'BUU-LSPINE's own paper was not found in Europe PMC'
reader_facts.fact: The paper is Klinwichit P, Yookwan W, Limchareon S, Chinnasarn K, Jang JS, Onuean A, 'BUU-LSPINE: A Thai Open Lumbar Spine Dataset for Spondylolisthesis Detection', Applied Sciences 2023;13(15):8646, 2023-07-27, CC BY, 36 citations on OpenAlex, 37 on Semantic Scholar; it is not indexed by Europe PMC and its only open copy is MDPI's, which refuses this container. The project page gives three releases: a 400-pair v0.1 sample (400 patients, 127 male, 273 female, ages 6 to 89, mean 50.2125; direct download), BUU-LSPINE(2000) with side-bending, rotation and flexion/extension labels (Google Drive), and BUU-LSPINE(3600) by a Google Form under an end-user licence agreement with the Faculty of Informatics, Burapha University; the annotation is the upper and lower edge lines of each lumbar vertebra as point coordinates in CSV with four listhesis diagnoses on the lower edges; JPG of various resolutions with no pixel spacing or mm statement; the GitHub README (North-Github/BUU-LSPINE) gives 3,600 patients, 7,200 images, 621 spondylolisthesis patients with 788 locations, 18.5 GB, a Google Drive folder, annotation by Burapha University Hospital physicians and radiologists, grant KSN1823130, and no licence.

reader_facts.row: Section 3, the SPIDER bullet's last sentence 'MRSpineSeg was not reached in this session'
reader_facts.fact: MRSpineSeg is the SpineParseNet dataset (Pang S et al., IEEE TMI 2021;40(1):262-273, 184 citations, closed): 215 subjects, T2 sagittal lumbar MRI, 19 structures (10 vertebrae and 9 discs), Dice 87.32, 87.78 and 87.49 percent; its challenge host www.spinesegmentation-challenge.com does not resolve from this session, and Sadu 2026 (Sci Rep, PMC13538668) [full] prints the labels as T9 to S with discs T9/T10 to L5/S in 20 classes, the voxel sizes and a 5-fold protocol of 43 subjects a fold; no licence was read anywhere.

reader_facts.row: Section 7 Gaps, the bullet listing Fujimori 2022, the npj Digital Medicine 2026 model, VLTENet, W-Transformer, KEF, Seg4Reg's LNCS paper, BUU-LSPINE, MRSpineSeg, Spinal-AI2024 and the EOS or Keops validations
reader_facts.fact: Every item in that bullet was reached in this sweep except the Seg4Reg LNCS abstract and the BUU-LSPINE full text (both closed to this container; see unreachable); Fujimori 2022 is now read in full (its reader comparison is 168 patients and 415 films, AI MAE 3.1 +/- 3.4 against surgeons at 3.9 and 3.8 deg, code MIT with ONNX weights), the npj paper is Kang et al. 2026 (PMC13031614), and the Spinal-AI2024 origin is CurvNet (arXiv 2411.12604).

reader_facts.row: Section 6, 'Settled' first bullet ('with code under MIT for one method (Yi 2020)') and the README row's 'Public code' cell ('1 with a licence')
reader_facts.fact: Two alignment methods now carry a licence: Yi 2020 (MIT) and Fujimori 2022 (github.com/ykszk/c2c7demo, MIT, copyright 2022 Yuki Suzuki, ONNX weights on Google Drive, a web demo at ykszk.github.io/c2c7demo); and the AASCE review links seven teams' repositories, the winner's Seg4Reg among them, none of which was read with a licence file (Seg4Reg's LICENSE answers 404).

[page]

facts.row: Natalia 2024 PLOS ONE, DeepLabv3 ResNet-50 + A* labelling [full] (section 2.3 bullet and table row)

The disc_w and disc_d line stays as it is but is now searched: the only automatic disc width (Liang 2024, sagittal, 33.1 mm mean) has no reader agreement, and the closest axial automation (Natalia 2020) measures a canal gap, not the disc. gaps.verifier_notes:
I checked each source myself. I used 3 WebFetch calls, 0 WebSearch calls and curl through the proxy. Every row came back corrected and none was refused. None of them repeats a method that discs.md already has in its table: MRSpineSeg, MICCAI 2015 and Spine Explorer appear in the note only as bullets.

Main corrections:
- Vemu: the rows put SVA and listhesis under 'MAE under 4.0 deg', but the abstract's Table 2 has angles only.
- Zheng 2017: the rows said 'no level labels', but the challenge's task is seven discs T11-S1. Its accepted manuscript can be read through figshare 29727326, not the 403 the reader met.
- Spine Explorer: the ICC 0.85-0.99 belongs to the paraspinal muscles only, and Huang 2020's anterior disc bulging area is an age correlation, not an ICC item.
- Kang and Liang: 'Private' is not stated, so it is now 'availability not stated'. Liang's 'mid-sagittal' is not stated; the source says sagittal view.
- Natalia 2020: the AP diameter definition and the setup of the single reader are made precise.
- MRSpineSeg: the 215 is volumetric MR of 215 subjects, not sagittal volumes. Lian's 172 are volumes, and its ATM-Net result is on Lian's own 8:1:1 split.
- Chamarthy: the link to NHANES II is only inferred from the co-authors. The PMID is 15127748.

Facts:
- BianqueNet: the reader's evidence was wrong, because the code sits under main/BianqueNet/ and even the root README answers 404. The licence is still unstated after checking that path.
- Hipp's supplement contents are listed in the article (Files S1 to S6), and the product is spelled Spine CAMP.

Everything I downloaded is under <session scratchpad>/verify-discs/ (subfolders v, zheng, olsia2). Nothing under /home/user/bordercall was touched.

facts.fact: Phadke et al., J Imaging 2026;12(8):388 (PMC13514485, CC BY): the ten morphometric descriptors from mid-sagittal polygon masks are disc height, disc height ratio (to the mean adjacent body height), upper body height, lower body height, spondylolisthesis offset (AP displacement of adjacent body centroids), offset ratio (to body depth), segmental angulation, disc AP width, disc-centroid-to-Posterior-A distance and disc-centroid-to-second-posterior-element distance, scaled by each DICOM's pixel spacing, with offset and angulation missing at L5-S1; truth is one expert reader, four grades; 468 patients and 2,978 foramina modelled, locked test 94 patients and 580 foramina (378/104/53/45), five-fold cross-validation on 374 patients; fusion QWK 0.813 (0.769 to 0.847), accuracy 0.753, adjacent accuracy 0.983, boundary AUROC 0.917, 0.953, 0.987; appearance-only QWK 0.806 (P 0.68), anatomy-only 0.444, level-and-side 0.314; code MIT at github.com/rohanpa27/LSS_foraminal_stenosis_imaging; transitional vertebrae not mentioned; ECE 0.106.

facts.row: SpineNetV2 (Windsor 2022) [page] (section 4) and its bullet in section 3
facts.reason: Printed: 'split 80:20:20% down the patient line'; demo T2 lumbar only https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2205.01683
facts.fact: Gradings on T2 lumbar discs: Pfirrmann (5), disc narrowing (4), central canal stenosis (4, also binary), upper and lower endplate defect (binary), upper and lower marrow change (binary), left and right foraminal stenosis (binary), spondylolisthesis (binary), herniation (binary) [full]. Level naming: no anchor counting, which the authors reject because it needs an anchor vertebra in view; a penalised beam search over an appearance network and a context network assigns labels from S1 up to C3 (the overview says C2), with penalties added in the case of transitional vertebrae or numerical variations, and double S1 or C3 detections relabelled in post-processing; L6, lumbosacral transitional vertebra and sacralisation are not named. Data: OWS, 710 sagittal whole-spine scans (719 in Figure 6) of 196 patients, S1 to C2 marked by a non-specialist; Genodisc, 2,279 patients and 2,819 lumbar T1/T2 scans from 6 centres (Figure 6), T2 graded by an expert radiologist; the public Zukic SpineWeb set, 17 scans, 154 vertebrae; splits printed as 80:20:20% down the patient line. Detection and labelling: OWS 37 test scans, 888 vertebrae, IDR 96.5%, LE 2.4 mm; Genodisc 421 scans, 2,947 vertebrae, IDR 98.4%, LE 1.6 mm; Zukic IDR 90.9%, LE 2.0 mm. Grading balanced accuracy V2: central canal binary 93.2% (V1 95.8%), four-class 64.9%, foraminal left 84.8%, right 82.4%, herniation 80.4%, Pfirrmann 70.9%, narrowing 76.3%; no kappa. The paper states no licence; a web demo accepts T2 lumbar scans only; a research tool, not for clinical use; detection and labelling of a whole spine take about 2 minutes on CPU, grading excluded.

facts.row: Lu 2018, DeepSPINE [full] (section 4) and its bullet in section 3
facts.reason: Criteria: 'number of detected vertebrae is the same as that of ground truth' https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1807.10215
facts.fact: The whole text never uses transitional, sacralisation, lumbarisation or L6 [full]; a lumbar detector (relatively rectangular boxes, T12 to L5) and a separately trained S1 detector (relatively trapezoidal boxes) are combined to name the six discs T12-L1 to L5-S1, and a segmentation counts as a success only when each detected area holds one true centroid, the detected vertebra count equals the truth and the S1 segment does not overlap a lumbar vertebra; how a six-lumbar spine would fare is not stated. The initial cohort was 7,108 examinations signed by 57 radiologists, reduced to 22,796 disc levels of 4,075 patients split 15,957/3,419/3,420; segmentation used 1,000 cases 60:20:20 with 188 of 200 test cases succeeding (94%); the stated limitations are the middle sagittal slice only, severe scoliosis and fused bodies, motion and metal artefact, and single-report labels with their inter-reader variability, highest for intermediate grades; the imbalance toward normal and the weaker mild and moderate grades are reported in the cohort and results, not as limitations; no data or code availability statement, only a supplementary video (bit.ly/DeepSPINE).

gaps.reader_notes: Settled, newly: the machine-made normative canal series is Gaonkar 2019 (AJNR), thecal sac area on axial MRI in 1,755 people at L1 to L5, correlated with height alone, Dice 0.84 against raters who agree at 0.90, with no per-level values and no data or code; SpineNetV2's level rule is now read (a beam search labelling S1 up to C2 with penalties for transitional vertebrae and numerical variations, IDR 96.5 to 98.4%, canal stenosis binary balanced accuracy 93.2% and four-class 64.9%, foraminal 82 to 85%) under Oxford VGG's own non-commercial terms rather than a standard licence; DeepSPINE never mentions a transitional vertebra and counts a six-lumbar spine as a detection failure; the licences are settled as Apache-2.0 (SPIDER baseline), MIT (CTM-DuraSeg, Phadke's code, the two Zenodo graders), none (Saravi's single notebook, TotalSpineSeg's README), CC BY 4.0 for the LSS-MRI data on Mendeley under a CC BY-NC-ND article whose boxes come from three neurosurgeons; and Phadke's ten descriptors are disc, body and listhesis measures in mm from one slice, none of which beat appearance alone. Not settled, unchanged: no CT method measures Panjabi's canal width or depth per level against public truth (three fetch-based searches, one arXiv query and one WebSearch found none; Huang 2025 is a CT foraminal grader, not a measurer), the VB-Net cervical CT paper stays unread, and no public canal chord truth with a named reader exists (Nixon's CC BY 4.0 deposit has no paper, counts or reader). New since the note: Kareem 2026's CC BY 4.0 central canal grades make the Sudirman 515 a public graded stenosis test set at three discs, an AISSLab axial set exists, and TotalSpineSeg joins SPIDER's code as a public canal segmenter that names levels without modelling transitional counts.

reader_facts.row: LSS-MRI-AISSLab and Phadke 2026 [code page, abstract] (section 4) and the LSS-MRI-AISSLab bullet (section 2)
reader_facts.fact: The dataset paper is Abdulmahmod et al., Sci Data 2026;13:809 (PMC13222877, PMID 41957051), article licence CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; the foraminal boxes were drawn by three neurosurgeons with 3, 11 and 26 years of experience, and the masks were validated and refined by three expert neurosurgeons (Figure 1's caption says neurologists); 500 patients, one examination each, 8,500 sagittal slices, 469 patients with at least one box, 2,979 boxes (1,396 right, 1,583 left; grades Normal 67.45%, Mild 17.06%, Moderate 8.53%, Severe 6.99%), so the GitHub About line's 3,885 is wrong; masks of vertebrae, discs, sacrum, Posterior A and Posterior B on 500 mid-sagittal slices; scanners Philips Ingenia 1.5 T and 3 T, GE Signa HDxt and Signa Excite 1.5 T; levels L1-L2 to L5-S1 with no numbering rule and no transitional mention; no inter-annotator agreement; the three-stage pipeline reached 86% slice selection, 90% ROI localisation and 65% severity accuracy, and SegResNet Dice 97.32%, HD95 2.337 mm; the article states no licence for the data or the code.

reader_facts.row: LSS-MRI-AISSLab and Phadke 2026 [code page, abstract] (section 4)
reader_facts.fact: The Mendeley deposit (version 4, 10 February 2026, DOI 10.17632/rgb77xm3jf.4) is licensed CC BY 4.0, so the data licence is CC BY 4.0 while the article is CC BY-NC-ND; the page repeats 500 patients, 8,500 slices and 2,979 boxes and names no annotator count.

reader_facts.row: LSS-MRI-AISSLab and Phadke 2026 [code page, abstract] (section 4) and the Phadke sentence in section 2
reader_facts.fact: Phadke et al., J Imaging 2026;12(8):388 (PMC13514485, CC BY): the ten morphometric descriptors from mid-sagittal polygon masks are disc height, disc height ratio (to the mean adjacent body height), upper body height, lower body height, spondylolisthesis offset (AP displacement of adjacent body centroids), offset ratio (to body depth), segmental angulation, disc AP width, disc-centroid-to-Posterior-A distance and disc-centroid-to-second-posterior-element distance, scaled by each DICOM's pixel spacing, with offset and angulation missing at L5-S1; truth is one expert reader, four grades; 468 patients and 2,978 foramina modelled, locked test 94 patients and 580 foramina (378/104/53/45), five-fold cross-validation on 374 patients; fusion QWK 0.813 (0.769 to 0.847), accuracy 0.753, adjacent accuracy 0.983, boundary AUROC 0.917, 0.953, 0.987; appearance-only QWK 0.806 (P 0.68), anatomy-only 0.444, level-and-side 0.314; code MIT at github.com/rohanpa27/LSS_foraminal_stenosis_imaging; transitional vertebrae not mentioned; ECE 0.106.

reader_facts.row: SpineNetV2 (Windsor 2022) [page] (section 4) and its bullet in section 3
reader_facts.fact: Gradings on T2 lumbar discs: Pfirrmann (5), disc narrowing (4), central canal stenosis (4, also binary), upper and lower endplate defect (binary), upper and lower marrow change (binary), left and right foraminal stenosis (binary), spondylolisthesis (binary), herniation (binary). Level naming: no anchor counting, which the authors say fails on missed detections and varying vertebra counts; a beam search over an appearance network and a context network assigns labels S1 up to C3 (the text elsewhere says C2), with penalties on sequences in the case of transitional vertebrae or numerical variations and on a missed level, and double S1 or C3 detections relabelled in post-processing; lumbosacral transitional vertebra, L6 and sacralisation are not named. Training sets: OWS, 710 sagittal whole-spine scans (719 in Figure 6) of 196 patients annotated S1 to C2 by a non-specialist; Genodisc, 2,279 patients, 2,819 lumbar T1/T2 scans from 6 centres with one expert radiologist's grades; the public Zukic SpineWeb set, 17 scans, 154 vertebrae; 80:20 splits by patient. Detection and labelling: OWS 37 test scans, 888 vertebrae, IDR 96.5%, LE 2.4 mm; Genodisc 421 scans, 2,947 vertebrae, IDR 98.4%, LE 1.6 mm; Zukic IDR 90.9%, LE 2.0 mm. Grading balanced accuracy V2: central canal binary 93.2% (V1 95.8%), four-class 64.9%, foraminal left 84.8%, right 82.4%, herniation 80.4%, Pfirrmann 70.9%, narrowing 76.3%; no kappa. The paper states no licence; the demo takes T2 lumbar scans on request; research tool, not for clinical use; whole-spine CPU run about 2 minutes.

reader_facts.row: SpineNetV2 (Windsor 2022) [page] (section 4), Code column
reader_facts.fact: The code's terms are the University of Oxford Visual Geometry Group's own terms of access in LICENCE.md, not a standard licence: strictly non-commercial research, outputs not for a commercial product, not a medical device, modified source distributable only with a substantial improvement and attribution, no recovery of training-data information; the README says a more permissive licence is available on request and asks for a citation of arXiv 2205.01683.

reader_facts.row: Lu 2018, DeepSPINE [full] (section 4) and its bullet in section 3
reader_facts.fact: The whole text never uses transitional, sacralisation, lumbarisation or L6; levels come from a lumbar detector (rectangular boxes) and a separate S1 detector (trapezoidal boxes) whose outputs are combined into the six discs T12-L1 to L5-S1, and a segmentation counts as a success only when the vertebra count matches the truth and S1 does not overlap a lumbar body, so a six-lumbar spine is a failure, not a named case; the initial cohort was 7,108 examinations signed by 57 radiologists, reduced to 22,796 disc levels of 4,075 patients split 15,957/3,419/3,420; segmentation used 1,000 cases 60:20:20 with 188 of 200 test cases succeeding (94%); limitations stated: the middle sagittal slice only, failure in severe scoliosis, fused bodies, motion and metal artefact, single-reader report labels and their inter-reader noise, weaker mild and moderate grades, imbalance toward normal; no data or code availability statement, only a demo video.

reader_facts.row: SPIDER baseline and nnU-Net (van der Graaf 2024) [full] (section 4), Code column
reader_facts.fact: The repository carries an Apache-2.0 LICENSE file (copyright line 2023 Diagnostic Image Analysis Group, Radboudumc); its README names no licence, no training set and no pretrained weights, and lists training and evaluation scripts (TrainSpine, TestSpine, EvaluateSpine) citing Lessmann et al., Medical Image Analysis 2019;53:142.

reader_facts.row: Fan 2024, CT myelogram dura [full] (section 4), Code column
reader_facts.fact: github.com/Huatsing-Lau/CTM-DuraSeg is MIT (copyright 2022 Huatsing-Lau); its README gives one inference script, main_inference2nrrd.py, running a trained 3D U-Net to NRRD, with tensorflow, keras, SimpleITK and pynrrd as dependencies, and lists no weight file, training code or data.

reader_facts.row: Saravi 2023 and Ghobrial 2025 [full] (section 4), Code column
reader_facts.fact: The Freiburg-AI-Research organisation holds 16 public repositories, none described as dural sac or stenosis work; the one that matches is Automated_DSCA_measurement (July 2023), a single notebook Code_Updated.ipynb in 3 commits with no README, no description, no licence and 0 stars; Saravi's data availability statement (PMC10525778) gives only the organisation URL and names no licence, so the code is public but unlicensed.

facts.row: Doerr 2020 EndSeg and SpNorm, CT [abstract]
facts.reason: The end-plate angle's own inter-reader CI95 is 5.8 degrees, not 6 to 8; the 128 DRRs include 30 repeats; the Munoz 2013 attribution was not at the page read. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7218103/
facts.fact: Doerr 2020 [full]: 7 patient CTs from SpineWeb Dataset 14, lateral and AP DRRs spanning C7 to S1, cases with normal or abnormal kyphosis and lordosis and no pathologically significant scoliosis; input is the CT plus one point label per vertebra placed by an expert radiologist at the approximate body centroid. Truth: five readers (two radiologists, three spinal neurosurgeons) marking a single end-plate per DRR on 128 DRRs (49 lateral and 49 AP plus 15 repeats of each); inter-reader CI95 5.8 degrees for the end-plate angle, and 8.2 proximal thoracic kyphosis, 6.0 main thoracic, 7.4 lumbar lordosis, 11.0, 8.2 and 4.8 coronal, mean inter-reader error 7.6 degrees over the alignment metrics. EndSeg's end-plate angle = slope of a line fitted to the projected end-plate points. Table 5 mean difference against manual at T2, T3, T4, T8, L1, L3, S1: EndSeg -3.6, -4.0, -2.2, 0.1, 0.4, 1.9, 0.8 degrees, average absolute difference 1.9 (t-test p = 0.33); SpNorm -2.1, -1.6, -0.4, 1.4, 2.6, 5.6, -5.3, average 2.7 (p = 0.83). 93.8 percent of both methods' end-plate angles inside the inter-reader CI95; alignment metrics mostly within 3.0 degrees, thoracic kyphosis up to about 6; region growing stable above tau about 5 degrees with error about 0.5 degree. No Dice or mm for the end-plate segmentation, no runtime, no code or data statement. Row cells become: 7 SpineWeb CTs, five readers on 128 DRRs; code not stated; average absolute end-plate angle difference 1.9 degrees (EndSeg) and 2.7 (SpNorm) over seven levels, readers' end-plate angle CI95 5.8 degrees.

gaps.reader_notes: Settled gains: Doerr 2020's per-end-plate angle on CT agrees with five readers to an average absolute 1.9 degrees over seven levels on seven SpineWeb CTs while the readers' own CI95 is 6 to 8 degrees, Vrtovec's observer floor for an end-plate tangent is about 1.0 to 1.4 degrees SD on CT or coronal MRI and 2.6 to 4.5 on sagittal MRI, and Jang's twelve raters spread 1.2 to 3.4 mm on film corners with end-plate angle RMSE 0.6 to 1.5 degrees, so Panjabi's 2 to 5 degree inclinations sit at the floor of what any reader or method resolves; a per-level end-plate width table in mm exists commercially (Medical Metrics' EPW scaling, 3,870 films, L1 to S1 all within 31.7 to 33.9 mm) and is used to scale films rather than to name levels, which is itself evidence that width alone separates lumbar levels poorly; Kishimoto's whole-column areas are a thresholded Mimics pipeline with no reliability, and Yao 2018 adds automatic width, depth and area for C3 to C7 with none, so EPAu and EPAl per level exist in tables with no error bar. Code: Spine-Morphology-Analyzer's Dimensions plugin and its SpineLib submodule do output upper and lower end-plate width and depth and an inter-vertebral angle from meshes (end-plates as faces within 45 degrees of the up vector), both still unlicensed; TPTBox (Apache-2.0) computes body widths and a per-vertebra sagittal wedge angle but no per-end-plate measure; Endplate3D-QCT's evaluation code scores masks and BMD only; no six-point DXA or film software outputs an end-plate width or depth. Not settled stays as it was: no public per-vertebra end-plate truth beyond Endplate3D-QCT's lumbar masks, Jang's labels are on request only and are not BUU-LSPINE, Feng's specimens and equations, Cappetti's end-plate dimensions and the BSPC framework's abstract remain unread, and Kishimoto's area-against-position relation is printed as r only, so using area to name a position needs re-derivation from its Table 1.

reader_rows.row_markdown: | Medical Metrics EPW scaling of lateral films by an assumed end-plate width per level (J Imaging Inform Med 2026) [full] | Not public: the assumed widths come from a proprietary 3,000 cervical and 870 lumbar films; tested on ring-calibrated films from 29 sites and 39 systems (117 cervical neutral, 109 cervical flexion-extension pairs, 196 lumbar neutral, 192 lumbar pairs) | No; algorithm and quality-control modules "protected by trade secrets" | Scale = assumed superior end-plate width over its measured pixels, taking the first level available in the order C5 15.11, C6 16.05, C4 14.92, C3 14.82, C7 16.52, C2 12.02 mm and L4 33.05, L5 32.81, L3 33.89, L1 31.74, S1 32.25 mm; absolute scale error against the ring 9.74 to 9.91 percent cervical and 7.51 to 7.69 percent lumbar, against 19.57 to 19.80 and 35.01 to 35.69 for the DICOM scale factor | Assumes the level to pick the width (automatic labelling, uncertain levels withheld), so it runs in the reverse direction to naming a level from a width; the one published per-level end-plate width table in mm from films, lateral view, no thoracic |
