unreachable: Automated Castellvi typing (posterior elements target 5): no method found after Europe PMC (Castellvi AND deep learning etc., 14 records; Bertolotti OR transitional vertebra AND machine learning, 180 hits, 15 read), OpenAlex (11 results) and one WebSearch; Kwak 2025 itself says no prior study focused on automated LSTV classification; the arXiv API timed out and then answered 503 and Semantic Scholar answered 429, so arXiv was not swept.

Automatic cervical or lumbar rib detector with data (target 3): none in Europe PMC's 48 hits (15 read) for cervical or lumbar rib with deep learning or automatic detection; only manual series (Sun 2025 UK Biobank, Duman 2026, Forseen 2015, Jankowski 2026) and the lumbar-rib meta-analysis were found.

A SPINEPS CT paper (target 6): none exists in OpenAlex's 25 results (the first two read, both MRI), the README cites no CT paper, and VERIDAH describes no CT segmentation model; api.github.com for the spineps releases answered 403 and gh refused (the repository is not attached to this session), so the CT model's release notes and the weights' licence stay unread.

A VerSe-based morphometry pipeline that outputs a spinous or transverse process length (target 7): none found on Europe PMC (51 hits, 14 read), one WebSearch, or OpenAlex; Paccini 2023 partitions VerSe vertebrae without measuring, Marzola 2026 measures the dens on 25 VerSe C2 vertebrae (abstract only), Gandia-Vano 2026 (PMC13297030) trains on VerSe 2020 and outputs finite-element fields, no dimension.

A pooled prevalence of eleven or thirteen rib pairs (target 10, second half): none among 1,530 Europe PMC hits for rib-number systematic reviews (10 read); only lumbar ribs (Osiowski 2024) and cervical ribs (Henry 2018) are pooled, and LSTV is pooled only narratively (Fang 2025).

www.spinesegmentation-challenge.com (MRSpineSeg's home, for its licence and label ids): the host does not resolve from this container and would have to be allowed in the session's network settings; the set was read through the SpineParseNet abstract, its GitHub README and three papers that use it.

Forseen 2015 (J Spine 4:222), Singer 1988 (Surg Radiol Anat 10:291-295), Singer 1989 (Clin Biomech 4:80-86), Hetherington 2017 and 2022, Pesteie 2015 and 2018, Henry 2018 (World Neurosurg), Nakajima 2026 (npj Digit Med) and Masharawi 2005 (Spine): abstracts only, their full texts behind OMICS, Springer, Elsevier, Nature and LWW pages this container does not read; Pal and Routal 1999 (J Anat) abstract only, no PMCID listed.

qims.amegroups.org answered 503 for Zhou 2023, which was then read in full on PMC (PMC10722060); the Gupta 2018 and Marzola 2024 PDFs came back as binary from WebFetch and were read with pdftotext in the scratchpad folder gaps-facets-posterior-counts.
Du Plessis 2022's data ("available on the University of Pretoria library website 2022") and Fang 2025's last 13,838 characters were not fetched.
gaps.reader_notes: Facets: the 510-vertebra study is Gupta 2018 (30 male dry columns, read in full) and its abrupt-or-gradual split is 46 against 54 on the right and 30 against 70 on the left, while Singer 1989 (630 CTs, 59.6 percent gradual), Forseen 2015 (244 CTs, 93 percent abrupt) and Pal and Routal 1999 (44 columns, 93 percent gradual) show the share is a matter of definition, so the Settled bullet's equal split should soften; Masharawi 2005's abstract gives shapes and side differences but no tropism magnitude; and the Not settled claim that no method names a level from a facet measure now reads as one manual CT attempt (Forseen 2015) that found the facet transition at the rib-defined T12 in only 75 percent, with Du Plessis 2022 giving the transitional vertebra's own facet angle (136 +/- 23 deg) between T12's and L1's. Posterior elements: nothing automatic measures the family still holds, but the ultrasound literature for anaesthesia (SLIDE, Pesteie, Chen 2026) and a public paired ultrasound-CT set (Cavalcanti 2025) exist, Jankowski 2026 scores a hand-measured transverse process length as a level cue across 11, 12 and 13 rib-bearing spines (fails 25 percent of typical and 70 percent of eleven-rib spines), VerSe-based substructure work (Paccini 2023, Marzola 2024 and 2026) outputs no process measure, no SPINEPS CT paper exists and the README's CT-only labels are the dens, sacral parts and metal, Di Angelo 2021's abstract confirms no dataset or rate, and VERIDAH and Zhou 2023 use no posterior element beyond a rater reading rib presence and Castellvi morphology. Counts: MRSpineSeg (215 T2 volumes, T9 to S, no variant class) joins SPIDER as a set that names levels by position; Yang 2025 (VerSe, T13 80 and L6 85 percent on a loosely described hold-out) and Nakajima 2026 (scoliosis films, 0.97 numbering on unspecified transitional vertebrae) are the first papers quoting a variant accuracy, neither a benchmark; the pooled prevalences are lumbar rib 2.1 percent, cervical rib 1.1 and LSTV 15.3 by narrative pooling, with none for 11 or 13 rib pairs, and five more reader-counted series (Forseen, Jankowski, Sun, Duman, Zhou) carry 2.6 to 2.9 percent eleven-rib and 1.6 to 3.2 percent four- or six-lumbar shares; automated Castellvi typing and an automatic cervical or lumbar rib detector remain not found after four routes each.
gaps.verifier_notes:
Every source was read at its own record: PubMed efetch and Europe PMC full-text XML through curl, the Gupta and Marzola PDFs with pdftotext, the arXiv HTML for Paccini and VERIDAH, OpenAlex, Crossref and Semantic Scholar for Forseen, and one WebFetch for Du Plessis (PMC9119610, not open in the API). No WebSearch was used. Files are in <session scratchpad>/verify-facets-posterior-counts/.

No row was refuted, two were held (Chen 2026, Marzola 2024) and the other 15 were corrected. The corrections that matter most:
- Forseen 2015: the abstract's rib-count denominators (7, 11, 234) sum to 252, not 244, and disagree with its own lowest-rib counts (8, 11, 225). The abstract also never says that segment 1 is C2.
- Jankowski 2026: Castellvi-positive spines were excluded only from the 17-spine C7T12L5 reference group. The 49 non-standard spines were included in full.
- Jankowski 2026 is already in counts-and-anomalies.md as "Lodz 2026". Zhou 2023 and Sun 2025 are already in SchwingNet's full-spine-corpora-with-reader-counted-variants.md, which section 1 cites.
- MRSpineSeg: Sadu 2026 says the challenge repository is no longer publicly accessible, so the set cannot be called public.
- Fang 2025: the 15.3 percent comes from 20 prevalence studies, not all 83.
- Cavalcanti 2025: the 6,091 labelled frames come from 9 of the 63 volunteers. The reader's per-sweep frame counts were not found in the text.
- Dana 2026: the 0.929 mAP50 is on crops cut from the ground-truth boxes. The full-spine 17-class detector scores 0.254.
- Pesteie 2015: 990 of 1,052 is 94 percent. The 90 percent figure is the leave-one-out accuracy.
- Rerunning the stated Castellvi Europe PMC query gives 97 hits, not 14.

Both Masharawi 2005 facts target text the note no longer carries: the review of 2026-10-30 already updated the row and the bullet to the PubMed abstract. The bullet fact is refuted as a duplicate, and the row fact is cut down to what is still missing.

Not verified: the reader's OpenAlex count (11) and web-search results, and the 1,530-hit rib-number review search, because the query was not given. The Yang Figure 5 per-level Dice image was not read.

reader_rows.name: Gupta 2018, the 510-vertebra facet study (facets target 2)
reader_rows.row_markdown: | Gupta, Singla, Agnihotri, Budhiraja, Goyal, Bansal 2018, Ann Int Med Dent Res 4(4):AT29-AT33, doi 10.21276/aimdr.2018.4.4.at6, CC BY-NC [full, journal PDF read by pdftotext] | No digital set. 30 adult male dry thoracolumbar columns (GMC Amritsar), boiled and labelled T1 to L5: 510 vertebrae (360 thoracic, 150 lumbar); the sagittal angle of the superior articular facet by a protractor, a steel wire in the midsagittal plane and a bent hairpin (Patel and Singel 2003) | No | Means only, no repeat or observer figure: thoracic 112 to 120 deg (T1 R 112.5, L 114.0; T6 L 120.3), T12 R 85, L 92.1 (ranges 30-125, 36-134), L1 R 32, L 34.2, L2 29, 29.8, L3 28.8, 28.6, L4 34.1, 32.1, L5 36.9, 40.4; left larger by 0.2 to 7 deg at every level but L4, not significant; T12 under 90 deg in 14 columns (46 percent) right and 9 (30) left; the change gradual over T11-L1 in 46 percent right and 30 left, over T10-L1 in 3.33, abrupt at T12-L1 in the rest; its Table 1 sets Pal 2000 and Patel 2004 (Indian, C3 to S1) beside it | 30 men, dry bone, no images, no age or sex analysis, no cervical, one protractor angle per facet, no transitional vertebra; the abstract's "almost equal number" is 46 against 54 on the right and 30 against 70 on the left |
reader_rows.where_in_note: facets.md, Table, after the row "Masharawi 2005 [abstract record]"
reader_rows.why_it_matters: It identifies and reads in full the study the note held only as a search summary, and shows that the abrupt-or-gradual share differs by side and is not the equal split the note's Settled section says.

reader_rows.name: Singer 1988 and 1989, CT facet orientation at the thoracolumbar junction
reader_rows.row_markdown: | Singer, Breidahl, Day 1988, Surg Radiol Anat 10(4):291-295 (PMID 3145570) and 1989, Clin Biomech 4(2):80-86 (PMID 23915998) [abstract, both] | No. 1988: 214 (176 abdominal CTs, 9 thoracolumbar junction referrals, 29 cadaveric columns), T11 to L2 on slices through the superior end-plates, joint angles by a computer-aided digitiser; 1989: 630 people aged 10 to 93 (551 abdominal CTs, 26 junction scans, 53 cadaveric spines), T10-11 to L1-2 | No | 1988: the mortice pattern (coronal superior, sagittal inferior) at T12 in 29 percent, T11 16, L1 0.5; gradual transition 54 percent; tropism over 20 deg at T11-12 21 percent, T12-L1 9. 1989: gradual over three levels (T10-11 to T12-L1) 59.6 percent; progressive T11-12 to L1-2 11.4, T9-10 to T11-12 0.5; abrupt at T11-12 to T12-L1 18.1, T10-11 to T11-12 10.2, T12-L1 to L1-2 0.2; asymmetry over 10 deg at T11-12 40.8 percent, T12-L1 17.7; L1 transverse process ossification anomalies 2.06 percent | The largest CT facet-orientation series at the junction (630 people) and the oldest; four levels, no per-level means in the abstracts, no data, no inter-observer figure, 1980s scanners; it shows the facet transition itself wanders over two segments, so a rule reading T12 from the facet angle meets that spread |
reader_rows.where_in_note: facets.md, Table, after the row "Van Schaik 1997 [abstract]"
reader_rows.why_it_matters: The note's classical CT prior art for facet_angle_axial and facet_tropism was one lower-lumbar series; these give the junction's transition and asymmetry shares in 630 people, the level signal a naming rule would read.

reader_rows.name: Du Plessis 2022, superior facet angle T11 to L1 and the transitional vertebra on CT
reader_rows.row_markdown: | Du Plessis and others 2022, J Anat 240(6):1179-1186, doi 10.1111/joa.13619 [full, PMC9119610] | Not open (the paper says the data would be on the University of Pretoria library website in 2022; not checked). 173 adults (175 in the Methods) aged 18 to 80, archived CTs, Windhoek, Namibia, 2018 to 2020; T11, T12, L1 and thoracolumbar transitional vertebrae only (most scans end there); the superior articular facet angle on axial CT in Syngo, reflex angles computed by hand | No | Means T11 184.5 +/- 8.16 deg, T12 182.8 +/- 10.4, L1 112.3 +/- 7.27, TLTV 136 +/- 23.18 (table SD 21.77); left and right not different at normal levels, the TLTV facets asymmetric; inter-observer correlation 0.978 to 0.997 over three observers on 10 repeated measurements; 13 or 14 TLTV (the text disagrees), each with another anomaly (hypoplastic ribs 8, spina bifida 5, sacralisation 4, lumbar numeric variation 6, compression fractures 4) | Three levels, one plane, by hand, no abrupt-or-gradual count of its own (it quotes Forseen 2015's 227 of 244 abrupt); the TLTV angle lies between T12's and L1's with twice the spread, which is the facet signature of the one vertebra a rule must not name wrong |
reader_rows.where_in_note: facets.md, Table, after the Singer 1988 and 1989 row (before "Simon 2012 [full]")
reader_rows.why_it_matters: It is the only CT series found that gives the facet angle of the thoracolumbar transitional vertebra itself, with per-level means and an observer figure.

reader_rows.name: Forseen 2015, the facet transition as a way of naming T12 on 244 CTs
reader_rows.row_markdown: | Forseen, Bruce, Gilbert, Patel, Ramirez, Borden 2015, J Spine 4:222, doi 10.4172/2165-7939.1000222, CC BY [abstract, OpenAlex record] | No. 244 whole-spine CTs; the facet transition (flat posterolateral to curved posteromedial superior facets) and the lowest rib-bearing segment read per patient, segments numbered caudally from C2 | No | Transition abrupt in 227 of 244 (93 percent); the transition at the 19th segment in 184 (75 percent), the 18th in 50 (20), the 20th in 10 (4); the lowest rib set at the 19th in 225 (92), the 20th 11 (5), the 18th 8 (3); eleven ribs in 7, thirteen in 11, twelve in 234, with lumbosacral transitional anatomy in 5 of 7, 8 of 11 and 24 of 234 (10 percent) | The one study that uses a facet feature to name a level, and it concludes the transition is not a reliable mark of T12 and that numbering must count caudally from C2; manual, no angle in degrees, no inter-reader figure, whether C2 is segment 1 or 2 not readable from the abstract, an OMICS journal |
reader_rows.where_in_note: facets.md, Table, after the Du Plessis 2022 row
reader_rows.why_it_matters: The note's Not settled section says no method names a level from a facet measure; this is the one that tried, by hand, and it disagrees with the rib-bearing segment in about a quarter of spines.

reader_rows.name: Pal and Routal 1999, abrupt versus gradual on 44 dry columns
reader_rows.row_markdown: - Pal and Routal 1999, J Anat 195(2):199-209, PMID 10529057 [abstract, Europe PMC]: 44 dry adult columns T9 to L5; the change of articular process orientation at the thoracolumbar junction abrupt in 3 columns (7 percent) and gradual over 2 or 3 successive vertebrae in 41 (93 percent), the reverse of Forseen 2015's 93 percent abrupt on CT and of Singer 1989's 59.6 percent gradual over three levels, so the two words are defined differently in different hands and no rule can take the share from the literature.
reader_rows.where_in_note: prose: facets.md, "Classical measurement of the family", after the Masharawi growth-paper bullet
reader_rows.why_it_matters: It shows the abrupt-or-gradual split, which the note calls settled as 80 to 20, runs from 7 to 93 percent abrupt depending on the definition and the material.

reader_rows.name: Jankowski 2026, the L3 transverse process length as a level landmark across counting variants
reader_rows.row_markdown: Jankowski and others, "Reliability of the L3 Transverse Process as a Landmark for Lumbar Spine Enumeration Across Different Vertebral Segmentation Patterns", Diagnostics 2026;16(20):3409, doi 10.3390/diagnostics16203409 (PMC13703058) [full] | On request only (ethical and privacy restrictions). 499 polytrauma whole-body CTs of one Polish tertiary hospital, 2022 to 2024, screened with confirmed numbering; the 49 non-standard formulas (C7T11L5 4, C7T11L6 6, C7T12L4 8, C7T12L6 18, C7T13L4 3, C7T13L5 10) and 17 C7T12L5 references analysed, 66 in all; Castellvi-positive spines excluded; counted by two final-year students, reviewed by a neurosurgeon, every case re-measured by a second neurosurgeon | None (manual multiplanar measurement) | Bilateral lumbar transverse process lengths from the pedicle-lamina junction to the tip; L3 the longest in 45 of 66 (68.2 percent) by single process and 49 of 66 (74.2) by bilateral mean; by thoracic pattern 30.0 / 30.0 (C7T11), 76.7 / 83.7 (C7T12), 69.2 / 76.9 (C7T13), the bilateral association holding after Holm correction (p 0.014); the 22nd presacral vertebra longest in 44 of 66 (66.7); inter-reader ICC 0.88 (0.85 to 0.91) single, 0.93 (0.90 to 0.94) bilateral | The one study that scores a posterior-element measure (transverse_length) as a level cue across 11, 12 and 13 rib-bearing patterns, by hand, and finds it fails a quarter of typical spines and 70 percent of eleven-rib spines; no automation, an enriched sample whose shares are not prevalences, no Castellvi case, CT only
reader_rows.where_in_note: posterior-elements.md, The table, after the row "Kwak, Ro and Kang, LSTV detection on lateral lumbar radiographs"
reader_rows.why_it_matters: It is the first reader-measured test found of whether a transverse process length carries level information in patients with count variants, which the note says nothing measures.

reader_rows.name: Chen 2026, two-stage U-Net and SVM on lumbar paramedian transverse ultrasound (posterior elements target 4)
reader_rows.row_markdown: Chen and others, two-stage U-Net and SVM for lumbar paramedian transverse ultrasound views (Front Radiol 2026;6:1721194, doi 10.3389/fradi.2026.1721194, PMC12936013) [full] | Not shareable (hospital permission; one centre, PUMCH). 425 patients, image count not given; 70 / 10 / 20 by patient; one anaesthesiologist annotated in LabelMe, a senior one reviewed, two checked independently | None stated; the article is CC BY | U-Net on the transverse process and the intervertebral foramen merged as one class, IoU 83.21 percent (a multi-class U-Net 77.33); an SVM on coordinate features classifies the two views at 97.66 percent (an end-to-end CNN 85.00); no Dice, no mm, no human comparison | Detects the transverse process to recognise a view, never to measure it; no lamina, no level named (the keywords say mid-lumbar), no transitional handling
reader_rows.where_in_note: posterior-elements.md, The table, after the row "Zeng and others, Stacked Hourglass landmarks on transverse ultrasound"
reader_rows.why_it_matters: It is the newest ultrasound transverse-process detector for anaesthesia with a full text, and it confirms that this literature finds a plane rather than measuring a process.

reader_rows.name: SLIDE (Hetherington 2017, 2022) and Pesteie 2015, 2018, ultrasound lamina and level identification for neuraxial anaesthesia
reader_rows.row_markdown: SLIDE, Hetherington and others (Int J Comput Assist Radiol Surg 2017, doi 10.1007/s11548-017-1575-8, PMID 28361323; Can J Anaesth 2022, doi 10.1007/s12630-022-02300-6, PMID 35941333) and Pesteie and others (IEEE Trans Med Imaging 2018, doi 10.1109/tmi.2017.2739110, PMID 28809679; Int J CARS 2015, PMID 26026697) [abstract, all four] | Not public. 2017: transverse lumbar ultrasound, training size not in the abstract, 20 test scans; 2022: 76 term parturients, the reference an experienced operator's traditional ultrasound (NCT02982317); 2018: expert sonographer annotations, counts not in the abstract; 2015: 1,090 epidural and 1,052 facet-joint images | None stated | 2017: a CNN with transfer learning and a state machine naming the level as the probe slides up from the sacrum, 88 percent (20-fold cross-validation), 17 of 20 test scans with every level right, 40 frames a second; 2022: agreement with the reference for L3-4 84 percent (Gwet AC1 0.82) against palpation 70 (0.59), adjusted odds ratio 2.99; 2018: epidural target error 1 mm lateral and 0.4 mm vertical in 3-D, 1.7 and 0.8 in 2-D; 2015: 94 percent (1,032 of 1,090) epidural and 90 (990 of 1,052) facet planes, 20 ms a frame | Names the interspace by counting from the sacrum, so it inherits every lumbosacral transitional vertebra and says nothing of them; lamina and spinous process are classes that find a plane, never measured; private data, no code, abstracts only here
reader_rows.where_in_note: posterior-elements.md, The table, after the Chen 2026 row
reader_rows.why_it_matters: These are the representative ultrasound methods the note's Gaps asked for; the one that names levels does so by counting from the sacrum and reports no transitional stratum.

reader_rows.name: Cavalcanti 2025, paired robotic and handheld lumbar ultrasound with CT (public)
reader_rows.row_markdown: Cavalcanti and others, paired robotic and handheld lumbar spine ultrasound with ground-truth CT (Sci Data 2025;12:1766, doi 10.1038/s41597-025-06047-9, PMC12603223) [full] | Public, CC BY 4.0, doi 10.48804/3XPCAE: 63 healthy volunteers aged 20 to 35 (39 women, 24 men); 223 handheld sweeps of about 2,700 frames and 375 robotic sweeps of 3,600 to 4,500 frames; 6,091 frames (2,353 handheld, 3,738 robotic) labelled with the bone surface by one physician, the figures showing spinous, mammillary and transverse processes and laminae; each volunteer's ultra-low-dose lumbar CT (CTDIvol 3.29 mGy) with L1 to L5 and S1 surface models | A U-Net baseline adapted from an open repository; no Dice reported | None for the labels (one annotator, no agreement figure) | The one public ultrasound set with posterior-element truth and a CT pair; lumbar only, young volunteers, the bone surface as one class with no per-structure label stated, frames not tagged by vertebral level in the text read
reader_rows.where_in_note: posterior-elements.md, The table, after the SLIDE and Pesteie row
reader_rows.why_it_matters: It is a public test set a lamina or process detector on ultrasound could be scored on, which the note's table lacked.

reader_rows.name: Dana 2026, YOLOv8 vertebra-level detection on thoracolumbar ultrasound
reader_rows.row_markdown: Dana, Zhang, Zheng, Ling, YOLOv8 vertebra-level completeness on thoracolumbar ultrasound (Sensors 2026;26(7):2101, doi 10.3390/s26072101, PMC13074876) [full] | Not public (ethical and privacy restrictions). 200 cases, 12 to 14 MHz linear B-mode sweeps of 10 to 40 frames; 160 / 40 by case; trained sonographers drew masks for T1 to T12 and L1 to L5, a second reviewer about 25 percent; how the levels were counted and whether checked against films not stated | None stated; the article is CC BY | 17-class crop model mAP50 0.929 (one-class 0.995); per-level accuracy 0.729 (T7) to 0.926 (T1), mean 0.91; per-scan completeness 0.74 | Scoliosis monitoring, not anaesthesia; the truth is a sonographer's count with no imaging reference, so no transitional vertebra can be scored; no measurement
reader_rows.where_in_note: posterior-elements.md, The table, after the Cavalcanti 2025 row
reader_rows.why_it_matters: It is the one ultrasound method found that names every level T1 to L5, and its truth has no anchor for a count variant.

reader_rows.name: Marzola 2024, enhanced statistical shape model with the AFRM feature recognition (Di Angelo's group)
reader_rows.row_markdown: Marzola, Di Angelo, Di Stefano, Volpe, "An enhanced statistical shape model for automatic feature segmentation of human vertebrae", Biomed Signal Process Control 2024;91:105972, doi 10.1016/j.bspc.2024.105972, CC BY-NC-ND [full, the Florence repository PDF read by pdftotext] | Confidential by its data statement. 25 pathologically unaffected L2 vertebrae segmented from SpineWeb CTs in Mimics, meshes at 1.25 mm; 20 train the eSSM, 5 healthy and 4 with features erased test it | None | Semantic labels (body, spinous process, lamina, left and right transverse processes, the articular facets) transferred from the AFRM's segmentation of the mean shape; the dimensional features of Di Angelo 2021 differ from the AFRM's by 0.01 to 11.68 percent on the five healthy tests, facet-centre distances 1.38 to 10.52 mm; the AFRM is the truth, so no reader | L2 only, adult male, mesh input (a segmentation first); the AFRM needs about 0.5 mm point clouds and every feature present; it is the group whose Di Angelo 2021 row the note could not read, and it names SpineWeb, not CSI 2014, as the source of its vertebrae
reader_rows.where_in_note: posterior-elements.md, The table, after the row "Di Angelo, Di Stefano and Guardiani ... 2021"
reader_rows.why_it_matters: It is the fullest readable account of the AFRM family that the note's Di Angelo row rests on, and it shows the method outputs dimensional features but is validated against itself.

reader_rows.name: Paccini 2023, VerSe-based partition of vertebrae into body, arch and processes (posterior elements target 7)
reader_rows.row_markdown: Paccini, Patane, Spagnuolo, "3D Patient-specific Modelling and Characterisation of Muscle-Skeletal Districts", arXiv 2304.14510 [full, arXiv HTML] | A VerSe'19 subset (the full set 160 series, 141 patients, 1,725 vertebrae; the subset size not stated), one scanner type; levels from VerSe's labels 1 to 24 plus 25 (L6) and 28 (T13) | None stated | Each vertebra mesh split into body, arch and processes by inflexion points of the distribution of vertex distances from the body centroid (thresholds T1, T2, T3; the text and Fig. 8 disagree on which separates arch from processes); outputs the thresholds and the mean HU of each region; validation qualitative (a fractured vertebra as an outlier), no Dice, no mm | A VerSe-based substructure partition that outputs no process length, height or angle; the only VerSe-based posterior-element work found, and it measures nothing of the family
reader_rows.where_in_note: posterior-elements.md, The table, after the Marzola 2024 row
reader_rows.why_it_matters: It answers the Gaps item on VerSe-based pipelines: the one found partitions the processes and measures nothing, so no public-mask pipeline outputs a process measure.

reader_rows.name: Yang 2025, WNet and ViT transitional-vertebra recognition on VerSe
reader_rows.row_markdown: Yang and others, transformer-enhanced vertebrae segmentation and anatomical variation recognition (Sci Rep 2025;15:34329, doi 10.1038/s41598-025-16689-9, PMC12491412, CC BY-NC-ND) [full] | VerSe 2019 and 2020, public, 374 CTs of 355 subjects; classes Normal, T13 and L6, the variant labels inferred from VerSe's centroid annotations (extra or missing counts), radiologists confirming only the shape classes; a 300-sample hold-out set the paper does not reconcile with VerSe's 53 transitional scans | The paper names github.com/anjany/verse (the challenge tooling) as its code; custom scripts on request | Mean Dice 0.953 (nnU-Net 0.921, SwinUNet 0.936), no Dice on variant cases; variant classification Normal 87 percent, L6 85, T13 80, AUC 0.95 / 0.96 / 0.93; age and sex fused into the classifier | A per-scan variant flag, not a labelling of the variant vertebra; the hold-out count and the three-class versus binary description conflict, the attention map is called simulated, no code of its own
reader_rows.where_in_note: counts-and-anomalies.md, section 2 table, after the row "Yeah T. and others, Dong Y., Angermann C. (VerSe'20 entrants)"
reader_rows.why_it_matters: It is the only VerSe-based paper found that reports a T13 and L6 recognition rate, and its truth and test set are too loosely described to count as a benchmark.

reader_rows.name: Nakajima 2026, CNN numbering on scoliosis radiographs with a transitional-vertebra accuracy
reader_rows.row_markdown: Nakajima and others, deep learning alignment and implant measurement on scoliosis radiographs (npj Digit Med 2026, doi 10.1038/s41746-026-03020-7, PMID 42469410) [abstract] | Not stated as public. 4,585 radiographs of 1,671 adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients, 10 institutions in 2 countries; training, validation and external test sets without sizes; the readers not in the abstract | Not stated | Major-curve Cobb MAE 2.7 deg (r 0.99), thoracic kyphosis 3.7 deg (r 0.91), implants 0.18 per image (r 0.99); vertebral numbering reaches an "accuracy of 0.97 for recognizing transitional vertebrae" | The one radiograph numbering result found that quotes a transitional-vertebra accuracy; which variant (lumbosacral, thoracolumbar, numerical) and how many cases are not in the abstract, the full text on nature.com is not readable here, adolescent scoliosis films only
reader_rows.where_in_note: counts-and-anomalies.md, section 2 table, after the row "Kwak 2025, LSTV present or absent on lateral lumbar radiographs"
reader_rows.why_it_matters: The note says no radiograph method reports a result on a transitional stratum; this one prints a number for it, though not what it counts.

reader_rows.name: MRSpineSeg challenge and SpineParseNet (counts target 9)
reader_rows.row_markdown: MRSpineSeg challenge and SpineParseNet, Pang 2021 (IEEE Trans Med Imaging 40(1):262-273, doi 10.1109/tmi.2020.3025087, PMID 32956047) [abstract for the paper; its dataset read in Sadu 2026 PMC13538668, Graf 2023 PMC10643734 and Yilizati-Yilihamu 2023 PMC10502997, all full] | Public through www.spinesegmentation-challenge.com (the 2nd CSIG Image and Graphics Technology Challenge; the host does not resolve from this container); 215 T2 sagittal lumbar MRI volumes from one local hospital, 172 released as training and validation; pixels 0.30 to 0.59 mm, slices 4.40 to 5.50 mm, 12 to 18 slices; 19 structures, the 10 vertebrae T9 to S and the 9 discs T9/T10 to L5/S, plus background; expert-corrected manual masks in ITK-SNAP; licence stated nowhere read | Yes, github.com/pangshumao/SpineParseNet, no licence named | SpineParseNet Dice 87.32 +/- 4.75 vertebrae, 87.78 +/- 4.64 discs, 87.49 +/- 3.81 over the 19; Sadu 2026 per level T9 38.74 to L1 92.89 and S 91.25 percent; Graf 2023 finds the masks exceed the bony borders and re-labels 20 volumes (Dice 0.77 to 0.80) | Fixed labels T9 to S with no L6 or T13 class and no transitional vertebra mentioned in any text read, so the lowest lumbar body is named by position above the sacrum; no count from C2; lumbar MRI only
reader_rows.where_in_note: counts-and-anomalies.md, section 2 table, after the row "SPIDER, van der Graaf 2024"
reader_rows.why_it_matters: It fills the note's MRSpineSeg gap: like SPIDER it names levels by position and carries no variant class.

reader_rows.name: Fang 2025, systematic review of LSTV prevalence (counts target 10)
reader_rows.row_markdown: Fang and others, systematic review and narrative analysis of lumbosacral transitional vertebrae (Brain Spine 2025;5:105628, doi 10.1016/j.bas.2025.105628, PMC12549404, CC BY) [full, first 100,000 characters] | 83 studies, searched to 2023-12-28; the prevalence analysis over 28,106 people with 4,290 LSTV | None | Mean prevalence 15.3 percent (4,290 of 28,106), range 4.5 to 35.6; narrative pooling only, no random-effects estimate, no confidence interval, no Castellvi or sacralisation-versus-lumbarisation split (Paik 2013's 10.6 percent types II to IV, 5.3 each, quoted alone); largest series French 2014 588 of 5,941 (9.9), Nardo 2012 841 of 4,636 (18.1), Tini 1977 269 of 4,000 (6.7), Hanhivaara 2020 1,101 of 3,855 (29) | A prevalence, not a method; the 4.5 to 35.6 range is the definition's and the cohort's, so a benchmark stratum needs its own definition before any pooled figure applies
reader_rows.where_in_note: counts-and-anomalies.md, section 2 table, after the row "BUU-LSPINE (Klinwichit 2023)"
reader_rows.why_it_matters: It is the closest thing to the pooled LSTV prevalence the README says was not found, and it declines to meta-analyse for heterogeneity.

reader_rows.name: Osiowski 2024 lumbar-rib meta-analysis and Henry 2018 cervical-rib meta-analysis
reader_rows.row_markdown: Osiowski and others, lumbar rib meta-analysis (Surg Radiol Anat 2024;46(12):2057-2066, doi 10.1007/s00276-024-03504-9, PMC11579145, CC BY) [full] and Henry and others, cervical rib meta-analysis (World Neurosurg 2018;110:e965-e978, doi 10.1016/j.wneu.2017.11.148, PMID 29203316) [abstract] | Osiowski: 9 studies, 5,430 people, 141 lumbar ribs, only series that counted the whole column (17 thoracolumbar vertebrae); Henry: 141 studies, 77,924 participants | None | Lumbar rib pooled 2.1 percent (95 percent CI 1.0 to 4.6), CT 1.6 (0.6 to 4.3; 4 studies, 2,906), radiograph 2.1 (0.4 to 11.1; 3 studies, 2,100), bilateral 65.4 (39.4 to 84.6), I2 90.11 to 97.16 in the subgroups, LFK index -4.55, random effects in MetaXL 5.3; cervical rib 1.1 percent in healthy people and 29.5 in thoracic outlet syndrome, no CI in the abstract | No pooled estimate exists for eleven or thirteen rib pairs (Europe PMC, 1,530 hits for rib-number reviews, the 10 read giving only Osiowski); the lumbar-rib definition excludes every spine with a count variant, which is the stratum a naming rule needs; neither tells a thirteenth rib from a lumbar rib by a stated length rule
reader_rows.where_in_note: counts-and-anomalies.md, section 2 table, after the Fang 2025 row
reader_rows.why_it_matters: They give the pooled figures the note lacked for two rib variants and show that the 11 and 13 pair question has no pooled answer.

reader_rows.name: Reader-counted series found on the way (Forseen 2015, Jankowski 2026, Sun 2025, Duman 2026, Zhou 2023)
reader_rows.row_markdown: - Four more reader-counted series and one count-only series, none open: Forseen 2015 [abstract] (244 whole-spine CTs: eleven ribs 7, thirteen 11, twelve 234, with lumbosacral transitional anatomy in 5 of 7, 8 of 11 and 24 of 234); Jankowski 2026 [full, PMC13703058] (499 trauma whole-body CTs with confirmed numbering: 49 non-standard formulas, 9.8 percent, C7T11L5 4, C7T11L6 6, C7T12L4 8, C7T12L6 18, C7T13L4 3, C7T13L5 10, Castellvi-positive spines excluded); Sun 2025 [full, PMC12630705, CC BY] (UK Biobank, 500 non-carriers counted by hand down from C2 on DXA and Dixon MRI, assuming 7 cervical and 12 thoracic: four lumbar 8, 1.6 percent, six lumbar 16, 3.2, eleven rib pairs 13, 2.6, L1 ribs 10, 2.0; the deep learning there only aligns DXA to MRI, code on GitHub, images by UK Biobank access); Duman 2026 [full, PMC13517915, CC BY] (517 thoracic CTs, one radiologist: hypoplastic twelfth rib 55, 10.64 percent, absent twelfth 22, 4.26, lumbar rib 12, 2.32, cervical rib 7, 1.35, any 96, 18.57, women 23.33 against men 14.44, p 0.013; no count method given, data on request); Zhou 2023 [full, PMC10722060, CC BY-NC-ND] (6,097 whole-body PET/CT screened, 450, 7.4 percent, with 23 or 25 presacral vertebrae, 211 and 239, 56 of them with a thoracolumbar transitional vertebra, 29 and 27, excluded; counted "from the cervical spine" by one musculoskeletal radiologist of 3 years, Castellvi read on the transverse processes, no posterior element segmented or measured, PACS VR and MPR, ICC over 0.8 but STA 0.639 to 0.875, no data statement).
reader_rows.where_in_note: prose: counts-and-anomalies.md, section 1, first bullet, after the sentence ending "no pooled meta-analysis was found before the search budget ended"
reader_rows.why_it_matters: They add five counted series, two of them with rib-pair counts, to the prevalence record the note pools from, and they settle what Zhou 2023 does with posterior elements (nothing).

reader_facts.row: facets.md, Table, row "Masharawi 2005 [abstract record] | Same collection; tropism and interfacet shape | No | Not readable | Not readable"
reader_facts.fact: The abstract is now read (PMID 15928537, doi 10.1097/01.brs.0000164098.00201.8d, Spine 2005;30(11):E281-92): 240 adult spines aged 20 to 80 of the Hamann-Todd collection, 4,080 vertebrae T1 to L5, a Microscribe 3-D digitiser; measures facet width, length, width-to-length ratio and interfacet distances; interarticular shape inverted trapezoidal at T1-T2, rectangular T3-L3, ordinary trapezoidal L4-L5; the left facet longer in the thoracic spine and the right in the lumbar; facet dimensions correlate with height and weight, larger in males, an ethnic component, age-independent; length flat across the thoracic levels and rising sharply through the lumbar; the distribution bipolar along the column; most facets longer than wide; no mm or degree is printed in the abstract. Accuracy cell: means and side differences by level, numbers not in the abstract. Lacks cell: dry bone, no images, T1 to L5, no transitional vertebrae, no angle, no interfacet height.

reader_facts.row: facets.md, "Classical measurement of the family", bullet "Masharawi 2005, Spine 30(11):E281-E292 [abstract record only, NEOMED library page; no numbers readable]"
reader_facts.fact: Read on Europe PMC and PubMed efetch: the abstract's only numbers are 240 spines, 4,080 vertebrae T1 to L5, ages 20 to 80, and the three shape ranges T1-T2, T3-L3, L4-L5; it says the left facet is longer in the thoracic spine and the right in the lumbar, that tropism is a normal characteristic that varies along the thoracolumbar spine, and gives no tropism magnitude in mm or degrees, so the per-level tropism table stays unread behind Spine's paywall.

reader_facts.row: facets.md, "What the family's prior art settles", Settled bullet "The thoracolumbar junction is bimodal in facet orientation (about 80 percent ... abrupt at T12-L1 or gradual over T11-L1 in near-equal shares in the 510-vertebra study ...)"
reader_facts.fact: The 510-vertebra study is Gupta and others 2018 (Ann Int Med Dent Res 4(4):AT29-AT33), 30 adult male dry columns; its shares are gradual over T11-L1 in 46 percent of columns on the right and 30 on the left, over T10-L1 in 3.33 percent on both sides, and abrupt at T12-L1 in the rest, so they are near-equal on the right only; and the share depends on the definition and the material: Forseen 2015 found 93 percent abrupt on 244 CTs, Pal and Routal 1999 93 percent gradual on 44 dry columns, Singer 1989 59.6 percent gradual over three levels on 630 CTs.

reader_facts.row: facets.md, Gaps, bullet "The 510-vertebra thoracolumbar facet study (360 thoracic, 150 lumbar) was seen only in a search summary and its page could not be identified for a fetch"
reader_facts.fact: Identified through OpenAlex (doi 10.21276/aimdr.2018.4.4.at6) and the journal's issue page, and read in full from the journal's PDF (CC BY-NC), so this bullet can go; the paper's own abstract says the change was abrupt or gradual "in almost equal number of columns" while its text gives 46 and 30 percent gradual over T11-L1 by side.

reader_facts.row: facets.md, "What the family's prior art settles", Not settled bullet "No method names a level from a facet measure, and no automatic pipeline covers the cervical facets, the whole column or a transitional vertebra"
reader_facts.fact: One manual method does: Forseen 2015 (J Spine 4:222) read the facet transition on 244 whole-spine CTs to identify T12 and found it at the 19th segment from C2 in 184 (75 percent), the 18th in 50 (20) and the 20th in 10 (4), against the lowest rib at the 19th in 225 (92 percent); it concludes the facet transition is not reliable and numbering must count from C2, which is the negative result a facet-based naming rule has to beat.

reader_facts.row: README.md, The families table, Facets row, "Closest to naming levels" cell ("no automatic CT or radiograph facet measurement exists, and no facet-based level naming anywhere")
reader_facts.fact: Facet-based level naming exists by hand: Forseen 2015 on 244 whole-spine CTs, where the facet transition marked the rib-defined T12 in about 75 percent and the authors rejected it as a landmark; Singer 1988 and 1989 (214 and 630 CTs) give the junction's transition and asymmetry shares, and Du Plessis 2022 (173 CTs) the facet angle of the thoracolumbar transitional vertebra itself, 136 +/- 23 deg between T12's 182.8 and L1's 112.3.

reader_facts.row: posterior-elements.md, The table, SPINEPS row ("the training data of the CT model are not named on the page" and "the weights' licence is not stated")
reader_facts.fact: The README read 2026-10-30 says a release "supports both CT and T2W" with completely independent, modality-specific models, lists CT-only labels 51 (Dens_axis), 70 to 74 (sacral ala left and right, posterior sacral elements, sacrum body, sacrum end-plate) and 80 (Metal), asks for two citations (the SPINEPS Eur Radiol 2024 paper, doi 10.1007/s00330-024-11155-y, and Graf 2023 Eur Radiol Exp, doi 10.1186/s41747-023-00385-2) and none for a CT paper; the code is Apache-2.0 and no licence is stated for the weights, which download from release pages; the GitHub API (403 for this session) could not give the release notes. The VERIDAH paper (arXiv 2601.14066) says its CT masks are in-house annotations supervised by an expert of 24 years and describes no CT segmentation model, no posterior-element label and no Dice.

reader_facts.row: posterior-elements.md, The table, row "Di Angelo, Di Stefano and Guardiani, An automatic method for feature segmentation of human thoracic and lumbar vertebrae, Comput Methods Programs Biomed 2021 ... [search]"
reader_facts.fact: The abstract is on Europe PMC (PMID 34517183, CMPB 2021;210:106360, doi 10.1016/j.cmpb.2021.106360, not open): input 3D high-density models from a 3D scanner or CT, "many real vertebrae" with no dataset name, no recognition rate and no mm figure printed, so the CSI 2014 attribution and the 99.8 and 94.1 percent rates stay a search summary; Marzola 2024 (same group, read in full) says the AFRM needs point clouds of about 0.5 mm and every feature present, and draws its own L2 vertebrae from SpineWeb CTs; the 2015 predecessor is CMPB 121(1):36-48 (PMID 25985887).

reader_facts.row: posterior-elements.md, Gaps, bullet "Not searched at all (budget): cervical or lumbar rib detection, ultrasound lamina or transverse-process detection for anaesthesia, an automated Castellvi typing method, a SPINEPS CT paper, VerSe-based morphometry pipelines that output process measures, the Zhou 2023 or VERIDAH posterior-element handling"
reader_facts.fact: Searched on 2026-10-30: no automatic cervical or lumbar rib detector exists in the records read (Europe PMC, 48 hits, 15 read; the nearest are Sun 2025's manual UK Biobank counts and Duman 2026's manual CT series); ultrasound lamina and transverse-process detection for anaesthesia is SLIDE, Pesteie 2015 and 2018, Chen 2026 and the public Cavalcanti 2025 set (rows above); no automated Castellvi typing was found on Europe PMC, OpenAlex or one web search, and Kwak 2025 states no prior study focused on automated LSTV classification; no SPINEPS CT paper exists (OpenAlex, the README's citations); the VerSe-based substructure work found (Paccini 2023; Marzola 2026's dens morphometry on 25 VerSe C2 vertebrae, doi 10.1007/s12008-026-02639-w, abstract only) outputs no process measure; Zhou 2023 and VERIDAH segment and measure no posterior element (VERIDAH's rater defines a thoracic vertebra by a true rib regardless of length and settles ambiguous cases by morphology such as facet orientation).

reader_facts.row: posterior-elements.md, "What the family's prior art settles and does not", Not settled sentence "No method handles a thirteenth rib pair, an eleventh, or a transitional vertebra's transverse process (the Castellvi types)"
reader_facts.fact: Still true of automatic methods; by hand, Jankowski 2026 measured lumbar transverse process lengths across 11, 12 and 13 rib-bearing patterns (L3 longest in 30.0, 76.7 and 69.2 percent by single process; ICC 0.88) and Forseen 2015 read the lowest rib and the facet transition on 244 CTs with 7 eleven-rib and 11 thirteen-rib spines, so reader-measured cues exist to score an automatic transverse_length against.

reader_facts.row: counts-and-anomalies.md, section 2 table, VERIDAH row ("a thoracic vertebra is defined by a true rib")
reader_facts.fact: The rib is read by the human rater, not by the model: the paper defines a thoracic vertebra as one having a true rib regardless of its length, settles ambiguous cases by morphology such as facet orientation, and adapts Konin's rule at the lumbosacral junction so that a vertebra with any Castellvi anomaly is a sacralised lumbar vertebra regardless of type; SPINEPS was trained for that distinction on the MRI data and hand-corrected in 16 cases (0.25 percent); the CT masks are in-house annotations supervised by an expert of 24 years, no CT segmentation model is described, no Dice is reported, and no licence is stated for the weights.

reader_facts.row: counts-and-anomalies.md, section 2 table, row "Castellvi typing by machine | No method found ..."
reader_facts.fact: Four routes on 2026-10-30 found none: Europe PMC (Castellvi with deep learning, automated classification or artificial intelligence: 14 records, only Kwak 2025), Europe PMC (Bertolotti or transitional vertebra with machine learning: 180 hits, 15 read, giving Kwak 2025, Yang 2025 and Nakajima 2026, none typing Castellvi), OpenAlex (11 results, none) and one web search (none; Kwak 2025 itself says no prior study focused on automated LSTV classification); the arXiv API timed out and then answered 503, and Semantic Scholar 429, so arXiv was not swept.

reader_facts.row: counts-and-anomalies.md, section 1, first bullet ("... no pooled meta-analysis was found before the search budget ended")
reader_facts.fact: Fang 2025 (Brain Spine 5:105628) pools 83 studies narratively, 4,290 LSTV in 28,106 people, 15.3 percent, range 4.5 to 35.6, with no random-effects estimate, interval or Castellvi split; Osiowski 2024 (Surg Radiol Anat 46:2057-2066) pools lumbar ribs at 2.1 percent (95 percent CI 1.0 to 4.6) over 9 studies and 5,430 people; Henry 2018 (World Neurosurg 110:e965-e978) pools cervical ribs at 1.1 percent over 141 studies and 77,924 people; no meta-analysis of eleven or thirteen rib pairs exists in the 1,530 Europe PMC hits for rib-number reviews (10 read).

reader_facts.row: counts-and-anomalies.md, section 4 Gaps, bullet "MRSpineSeg (Pang 2021) was not reached at all (the search returned SPIDER); its label scheme and any L6 are unread"
reader_facts.fact: Read on 2026-10-30 through the SpineParseNet abstract (PMID 32956047) and three papers that use the set (Sadu 2026, Graf 2023, Yilizati-Yilihamu 2023): 215 T2 sagittal lumbar volumes, 172 released, 19 structures (vertebrae T9 to S, discs T9/T10 to L5/S), no L6 or T13 class and no transitional vertebra mentioned; the challenge site www.spinesegmentation-challenge.com does not resolve from this container, so the licence and label ids are unread at source; the SpineParseNet README names no licence.

reader_facts.row: counts-and-anomalies.md, section 4 Gaps, bullet "Searches not run (budget exhausted after 17): TotalSpineSeg variant handling, thoracolumbar transitional or lumbar-rib detectors on CT, automatic Castellvi grading, Chen D 2020's L6 treatment, cervical-rib AI with data, AASCE and NHANES II for count truth, MRSpineSeg"
reader_facts.fact: Run on 2026-10-30 for automatic Castellvi grading (none), cervical-rib AI with data (none; the ACR use case stands), lumbar-rib detectors (none automatic; Osiowski 2024 pools manual series) and MRSpineSeg (read); TotalSpineSeg variant handling, Chen D 2020's L6 treatment and AASCE or NHANES II count truth were not searched again.

reader_facts.row: README.md, The families table, Counts and anomalies row, "Closest to naming levels" cell ("no pooled prevalence meta-analysis")
reader_facts.fact: Pooled figures now exist for two variants and not for the counts: lumbar ribs 2.1 percent (Osiowski 2024, 9 studies), cervical ribs 1.1 percent (Henry 2018, 141 studies), LSTV 15.3 percent by narrative pooling of 83 studies without an interval (Fang 2025); none pools eleven or thirteen rib pairs or four or six lumbar vertebrae.

reader_facts.row: counts-and-anomalies.md, section 2 table, row "Cervical rib detection: ACR AI use case (CT; a sibling for MRI) [page]"
reader_facts.fact: Still no algorithm or dataset on 2026-10-30 (Europe PMC, 48 hits for cervical or lumbar rib with deep learning or automatic detection, none a detector); the prevalence to design against is Henry 2018's pooled 1.1 percent in healthy people (141 studies, 77,924 participants, more than half unilateral), and Duman 2026 found 7 of 517 (1.35 percent) on thoracic CT by one reader.
